def test_archive_then_restore_roundtrip(self, kl, tmp_repo_with_cogz):
        """archive_knowledge and restore_archived should maintain file-DB consistency."""
        kid = kl.create("architecture", "Archive Me", "Content to archive",
                       repo_path=tmp_repo_with_cogz)
        entry = kl.get(kid)
        assert entry["consolidation_status"] == "active"

        # Archive
        result = kl.archive_knowledge(kid)
        assert result is True
        entry = kl.get(kid)
        assert entry["consolidation_status"] == "archived"
        # File should be in archive dir
        archive_files = list((tmp_repo_with_cogz / ".cogz" / "knowledge" / "archive" / "architecture").iterdir())
        assert len(archive_files) == 1
        # File should NOT be in active dir
        active_files = list((tmp_repo_with_cogz / ".cogz" / "knowledge" / "architecture").iterdir())
        assert len(active_files) == 0

        # Restore
        result = kl.restore_archived(kid)
        assert result is True
        entry = kl.get(kid)
        assert entry["consolidation_status"] == "active"
        # File should be back in active dir
        active_files = list((tmp_repo_with_cogz / ".cogz" / "knowledge" / "architecture").iterdir())
        assert len(active_files) == 1
        # File should NOT be in archive dir
        archive_files = list((tmp_repo_with_cogz / ".cogz" / "knowledge" / "archive" / "architecture").iterdir())
        assert len(archive_files) == 0

def _promote_rule(self, rule: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
        """Promote a single validated rule to canonical knowledge.

        Args:
            rule: The rule record from the learning layer.

        Returns:
            Promotion result dict or None if promotion failed.
        """
        statement = rule.get("statement", "")
        rule_id = rule["id"]
        confidence = rule.get("confidence", 0.5)

        # Build knowledge content
        content_lines = [
            f"# Rule: {statement}",
            "",
            f"**Confidence:** {confidence:.2f}",
            f"**Rule ID:** {rule_id}",
            "",
            "## Evidence",
        ]

        obs_ids = rule.get("supporting_observation_ids", [])
        if isinstance(obs_ids, str):
            import json as _json
            obs_ids = _json.loads(obs_ids)
        if obs_ids:
            content_lines.append(f"- Supporting observations: {', '.join(obs_ids)}")

        exp_ids = rule.get("supporting_experiment_ids", [])
        if isinstance(exp_ids, str):
            import json as _json
            exp_ids = _json.loads(exp_ids)
        if exp_ids:
            content_lines.append(f"- Supporting experiments: {', '.join(exp_ids)}")

        content_lines.extend(["", "## Status", "- VALIDATED", ""])
        content = "\n".join(content_lines)

def archive_knowledge(self, knowledge_id: str) -> bool:
        """Move a knowledge file to the archive/ directory and mark it archived.

        The file is moved from its current location (authored or auto) to
        ``.cogz/knowledge/archive/{type}/``.  The DB record's
        ``consolidation_status`` is set to ``"archived"`` and the file is
        no longer synced.

        Returns True if archived, False if not found or already archived.
        """
        if self.repo_path is None:
            return False
        entry = self.storage._get("knowledge", knowledge_id)
        if not entry:
            return False
        status = entry.get("consolidation_status", "active")
        if status == "archived":
            return False

        ktype = entry.get("type", "knowledge")
        title = entry.get("title", "")
        fmt = entry.get("format", "markdown")
        auto = bool(entry.get("auto_generated", 0))
        filename = self.compute_filename(knowledge_id, title, fmt)

        # Find current file
        current_dir = self._knowledge_dir(ktype, auto=auto)
        if current_dir is None:
            return False
        current_path = current_dir / filename
        if not current_path.exists():
            # Try source_path from DB
            sp = entry.get("source_path")
            if sp:
                current_path = Path(sp)
            if not current_path.exists():
                return False

        # Move to archive
        archive_dir = self.repo_path / ".cogz" / "knowledge" / "archive" / ktype

def restore_archived(self, knowledge_id: str) -> bool:
        """Restore an archived knowledge file to its active location.

        Moves the file from archive/ back to its authored/auto namespace
        and sets ``consolidation_status`` back to ``"active"``.

        Returns True if restored, False if not found or not archived.
        """
        if self.repo_path is None:
            return False
        entry = self.storage._get("knowledge", knowledge_id)
        if not entry:
            return False
        status = entry.get("consolidation_status", "active")
        if status != "archived":
            return False

        ktype = entry.get("type", "knowledge")
        title = entry.get("title", "")
        fmt = entry.get("format", "markdown")
        auto = bool(entry.get("auto_generated", 0))
        filename = self.compute_filename(knowledge_id, title, fmt)

        # Find archived file
        archive_dir = self.repo_path / ".cogz" / "knowledge" / "archive" / ktype
        archive_path = archive_dir / filename
        if not archive_path.exists():
            # Try source_path from DB
            sp = entry.get("source_path")
            if sp:
                archive_path = Path(sp)
            if not archive_path.exists():
                return False

        # Move back to active location
        target_dir = self._knowledge_dir(ktype, auto=auto)
        if target_dir is None:
            return False
        target_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        target_path = target_dir / filename

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Git merge driver for CogZ knowledge files (Phase 3.5).

Installed via .gitattributes:
    .cogz/knowledge/**/*.md merge=cogz-knowledge

The merge driver is invoked by git with three arguments:
    %O - the ancestor (common base) version
    %A - the current branch (ours) version
    %B - the other branch (theirs) version

The driver:
1. Parses metadata headers from all three versions.
2. If IDs match, compares versions and content hashes.
   - If one is strictly newer (higher version), keep it.
   - If versions are equal but content differs, produce a conflict file
     with both versions for manual review.
3. If IDs differ, both files are kept (they are different knowledge
   entries that happen to share a filename — rename one).

Exit codes:
    0: merge succeeded (output written to %A)
    1: conflict (conflict markers written to %A)

def get_stats(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Get comprehensive system statistics.

        This is the canonical stats method used by API, MCP, and CLI.
        """
        graph_stats = self.graph.get_stats()
        with self.storage._connect() as conn:
            counts = {
                "tasks": conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tasks").fetchone()[0],
                "plans": conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM plans").fetchone()[0],
                "sessions": conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions").fetchone()[0],
                "validation_runs": conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM validation_runs").fetchone()[0],
                "predictions": conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM predictions").fetchone()[0],
                "outcomes": conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM outcomes").fetchone()[0],
                "observations": conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM observations").fetchone()[0],
                "experiments": conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM experiments").fetchone()[0],
                "rules": conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM rules").fetchone()[0],
                "knowledge": conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM knowledge").fetchone()[0],
            }
            avg_confidence = conn.execute(
                "SELECT AVG(confidence) FROM predictions"
            ).fetchone()[0] or 0.0
            rule_confidences = conn.execute(
                "SELECT confidence, COUNT(*) FROM rules GROUP BY confidence"
            ).fetchall()
        return {
            **graph_stats,
            **counts,
            "avg_prediction_confidence": round(avg_confidence, 4),
            "rule_confidence_distribution": {
                str(r["confidence"]): r["COUNT(*)"] for r in rule_confidences
            },
        }

async def _call_process(self, name: str, arguments: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        from mcp import ClientSession, StdioServerParameters
        from mcp.client.stdio import stdio_client

        env = dict(os.environ)
        env["COGZ_DB"] = str(self.db_path)
        if self.repo_path is not None:
            env["COGZ_REPO"] = str(self.repo_path)
        params = StdioServerParameters(
            command=sys.executable,
            args=["-m", "cogz.cli", "mcp-stdio"],
            env=env,
        )
        async with stdio_client(params) as (read, write):
            async with ClientSession(read, write) as session:
                await session.initialize()
                result = await session.call_tool(name, arguments)
        if not result.content:
            return {}
        text = result.content[0].text
        parsed = json.loads(text)
        return parsed if isinstance(parsed, dict) else {"value": parsed}

"""Git merge driver for CogZ knowledge files (Phase 3.5).

Installed via .gitattributes:
    .cogz/knowledge/**/*.md merge=cogz-knowledge

The merge driver is invoked by git with three arguments:
    %O - the ancestor (common base) version
    %A - the current branch (ours) version
    %B - the other branch (theirs) version

The driver:
1. Parses metadata headers from all three versions.
2. If IDs match, compares versions and content hashes.
   - If one is strictly newer (higher version), keep it.
   - If versions are equal but content differs, produce a conflict file
     with both versions for manual review.
3. If IDs differ, both files are kept (they are different knowledge
   entries that happen to share a filename — rename one).

Exit codes:
    0: merge succeeded (output written to %A)

def _merge_duplicate_result(
        self,
        r: RetrievalResult,
        deduped: list[RetrievalResult],
    ) -> None:
        """Merge a duplicate result into the deduped list in place.

        If the existing entry is a "node" type, replace it with the
        specific-type version, preserving the higher relevance score.
        """
        for i, existing in enumerate(deduped):
            if existing.entity_id == r.entity_id and existing.entity_type == "node":
                if r.relevance_score < existing.relevance_score:
                    r = RetrievalResult(
                        entity_type=r.entity_type,
                        entity_id=r.entity_id,
                        text=r.text,
                        relevance_score=existing.relevance_score,
                        project=r.project,
                        subcategory=r.subcategory,
                        domain=r.domain,
                        semantic_score=r.semantic_score,
                        recency_score=r.recency_score,
                        importance_score=r.importance_score,
                        access_score=r.access_score,
                        graph_score=r.graph_score,
                        expansion_path=r.expansion_path,
                        hop_count=r.hop_count,
                        explanation=r.explanation,
                    )
                deduped[i] = r
                break

def _merge_duplicate_result(
        self,
        r: RetrievalResult,
        deduped: list[RetrievalResult],
    ) -> None:
        """Merge a duplicate result into the deduped list in place.

        If the existing entry is a "node" type, replace it with the
        specific-type version, preserving the higher relevance score.
        """
        for i, existing in enumerate(deduped):
            if existing.entity_id == r.entity_id and existing.entity_type == "node":
                if r.relevance_score < existing.relevance_score:
                    r = RetrievalResult(
                        entity_type=r.entity_type,
                        entity_id=r.entity_id,
                        text=r.text,
                        relevance_score=existing.relevance_score,
                        project=r.project,
                        subcategory=r.subcategory,
                        domain=r.domain,
                        semantic_score=r.semantic_score,
                        recency_score=r.recency_score,
                        importance_score=r.importance_score,
                        access_score=r.access_score,
                        graph_score=r.graph_score,
                        expansion_path=r.expansion_path,
                        hop_count=r.hop_count,
                        explanation=r.explanation,
                    )
                deduped[i] = r
                break

"""Graph algorithm library for CogZ.

Pure Python implementations of graph algorithms for architectural analysis.
No external dependencies (NetworkX, igraph, etc.) at runtime.

Target scale: 1K-10K nodes, 2K-20K edges.
All algorithms load the graph into an in-memory adjacency list, run, and

def _fix_consolidation_lineage(self, issues: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> int:
        """Remove orphaned supersedes edges."""
        fixed = 0
        with self.storage._connect() as conn:
            for issue in issues:
                edge_id = issue.get("edge_id")
                if edge_id:
                    conn.execute("DELETE FROM edges WHERE id = ?", (edge_id,))
                    fixed += 1
            conn.commit()
        return fixed

def gate_consolidation_ran(
    consolidate_response: dict[str, Any],
    execution_surface: str = "",
    seed: int | None = None,
    environment: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> GateResult:
    """Verify that consolidation completed without errors."""
    errors = consolidate_response.get("errors", [])
    completed = consolidate_response.get("status") != "error" and not errors
    return GateResult(
        name="consolidation_completed",
        passed=completed,
        value=len(errors),
        threshold=0,
        message=f"Consolidation completed with {len(errors)} errors" + (f": {errors}" if errors else ""),
        numerator=0 if errors else 1,
        denominator=1,
        observed_ids=[],
        expected_ids=[],
        execution_surface=execution_surface,
        seed=seed,
        environment=environment or {},
    )

def generate_report(all_metrics: list[E2EMetrics], output_path: Path) -> None:
    """Generate markdown report for combined e2e results."""
    lines = [
        "# Combined End-to-End Benchmark Results",
        "",
        f"**Date**: {time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S UTC', time.gmtime())}",
        "",
        "## Per-Tier Configuration",
        "",
    ]

    # Config table
    for tier, config in TIER_CONFIGS.items():
        lines.extend([
            f"### {tier}",
            f"- **Description**: {config['description']}",
            f"- **Embedding**: {config['embedding_model'] or 'none (FTS-only)'}",
            f"- **Reranker**: {config['reranker_model'] or 'none'}",
            f"- **Graph expansion**: {config['graph_expansion_hops']}-hop, edge-type weighted",
            f"- **Context weighting**: {'context-aware' if config['context_dependent_weights'] else 'fixed'}",
            f"- **Context pack**: k={config['context_pack_k']}, compress={config['context_pack_compress']}",
            "",
        ])

    # Results table per dataset
    datasets = sorted(set(m.dataset_name for m in all_metrics))
    for ds_name in datasets:
        ds_metrics = [m for m in all_metrics if m.dataset_name == ds_name]
        lines.extend([
            f"## {ds_name}",
            "",

def validate_config(config: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Validate a config dict against the schema.

    Returns a dict with:
      - ``valid``: bool — True if no errors
      - ``errors``: list[str] — validation error messages
      - ``warnings``: list[str] — non-fatal issues (unknown keys, etc.)
    """
    errors: list[str] = []
    warnings: list[str] = []

    for key, spec in CONFIG_SCHEMA.items():
        if key not in config:
            continue  # missing keys use defaults
        value = config[key]
        expected_type = spec["type"]
        if not isinstance(value, expected_type):
            errors.append(
                f"{key}: expected {expected_type.__name__}, got {type(value).__name__}"
            )
            continue
        # Check sub-fields
        _validate_sub_fields(key, value, spec, errors)

    # Check for unknown top-level keys
    known_keys = set(CONFIG_SCHEMA.keys())
    for key in config:
        if key not in known_keys:
            warnings.append(f"Unknown top-level key: '{key}'")

    # Validate default_provider if set
    provider = config.get("default_provider")
    if provider and provider not in CONFIG_SCHEMA["default_provider"]["allowed"]:
        errors.append(
            f"default_provider: '{provider}' is not in "
            f"allowed values {CONFIG_SCHEMA['default_provider']['allowed']}"
        )

    # Validate provider configs have required fields
    _validate_providers(config, errors, warnings)

def _load_all(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Load configuration from all sources with priority."""
        config: dict[str, Any] = {}

        # 5. Built-in defaults
        config.update(DEFAULT_CONFIG)

        # 4. Environment variables (provider name)
        env_provider = os.getenv("COGZ_PROVIDER")
        if env_provider:
            config["default_provider"] = env_provider

        # 3. Global config
        global_cfg = self._load_yaml(self._global_config_path())
        if global_cfg:
            self._strip_legacy_tier(global_cfg)
            config = self._merge(config, global_cfg)

        # 2. Project config
        proj_path = self._project_config_path()
        if proj_path:
            proj_cfg = self._load_yaml(proj_path)
            if proj_cfg:
                self._strip_legacy_tier(proj_cfg)
                config = self._merge(config, proj_cfg)

            # 2b. Hardware profile (saved by cogz init) — loaded for
            # capability display only; does not affect model selection.
            hw_path = proj_path.parent / "hardware-profile.yaml"
            hw_cfg = self._load_yaml(hw_path)
            if hw_cfg:
                hw_cfg.pop("tier", None)  # legacy field, stripped on load
                config.setdefault("hardware", {}).update(hw_cfg)

        # 1. Runtime overrides (highest priority)
        config = self._merge(config, self._overrides)

        return config

def test_config_set_persists_overlay_only(tmp_db, tmp_repo):
    """config set must save only the set key, not the full resolved config.
    Baking in defaults would prevent future DEFAULT_CONFIG changes from
    taking effect on projects that have run config set."""
    import yaml
    runner = CliRunner()
    runner.invoke(cli, ["--db", str(tmp_db), "--repo", str(tmp_repo), "init"])
    result = runner.invoke(cli, [
        "--db", str(tmp_db), "--repo", str(tmp_repo),
        "config", "telemetry.enabled", "true",
    ])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    config_path = tmp_repo / ".cogz" / "config" / "models.yaml"
    assert config_path.exists()
    saved = yaml.safe_load(config_path.read_text())
    assert saved.get("telemetry", {}).get("enabled") is True
    # Defaults must NOT be baked in
    assert "providers" not in saved, "config set baked in provider defaults"
    assert "default_provider" not in saved, "config set baked in default_provider"
    assert "embedding" not in saved, "config set baked in embedding defaults"

def _insert(self, table: str, data: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
        self._validate_table(table)
        self._validate_columns(data)
        # Serialize dict/list values to JSON strings for SQLite storage
        data = {k: json.dumps(v) if isinstance(v, (dict, list)) else v for k, v in data.items()}
        cols = ", ".join(data.keys())
        placeholders = ", ".join(["?"] * len(data))
        with self._connect() as conn:
            conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO {table} ({cols}) VALUES ({placeholders})", tuple(data.values()))
            if not self._in_transaction:
                conn.commit()
        return data["id"]

sections.content:
def _auto_widen(
        self,
        query: str,
        top_k: int,
        options: SearchOptions,
        current: list[SearchResult],
    ) -> list[SearchResult]:
        """Progressively relax taxonomy filters to find more results.

        Three levels: drop domain → drop subcategory → drop project.
        Stops as soon as enough results are found.
        """
        fused = current
        seen = {(r.entity_type, r.entity_id) for r in fused}

        def _merge(wider: list[SearchResult]) -> None:
            nonlocal fused
            for r in wider:
                if (r.entity_type, r.entity_id) not in seen:
                    fused.append(r)
                    seen.add((r.entity_type, r.entity_id))

        # Level 1: drop domain
        if options.domain is not None and len(fused) < SEARCH_AUTO_WIDEN_THRESHOLD:
            wider = self.search(
                query, top_k, options.project, options.subcategory, None, options.entity_types,
                mode=options.mode, rerank=False, auto_widen=False,
                snippet_chars=options.snippet_chars,
                include_superseded=options.include_superseded,
            )
            for r in wider:
                r.scope_relaxation = "domain"
            _merge(wider)

        # Level 2: drop subcategory
        if options.subcategory is not None and len(fused) < SEARCH_AUTO_WIDEN_THRESHOLD:
            wider = self.search(
                query, top_k, options.project, None, options.domain, options.entity_types,
                mode=options.mode, rerank=False, auto_widen=False,
                snippet_chars=options.snippet_chars,

"""Search engine for CogZ (Phase 1B).

Hybrid search combining FTS5 (keyword) and vector (semantic) search
with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF). Auto-widens the search scope when
initial results are insufficient.

Flow:
  1. FTS5 search on all text-bearing tables (BM25 ranked)
     - Natural language queries are rewritten to FTS5 OR syntax
       to avoid implicit AND matching all terms (which rarely
       matches any document with multi-word questions).
  2. Vector search on vec_entities (cosine distance via sqlite-vec)
  3. RRF fusion of both result sets
  4. Optional reranker cross-encoder reranking

Auto-widen: if initial results < threshold, relax taxonomy filters
in three levels: drop domain, then subcategory, then project.

class SearchEngine:
    """Hybrid search engine combining FTS5 and vector search.

    Args:
        storage: The Storage instance.
        embedding: Optional EmbeddingEngine for vector search (code entities).
        knowledge_embedding: Optional EmbeddingEngine for non-code entities
            (observations, rules, patterns). Falls back to `embedding` if None.
        reranker: Optional RerankerEngine for cross-encoder reranking.
        splitter: Optional TextSplitter for chunk-level search.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        storage: Storage,
        embedding=None,
        knowledge_embedding=None,
        reranker: RerankerEngine | None = None,
        splitter: TextSplitter | None = None,
    ):
        self.storage = storage
        self.embedding = embedding
        self.knowledge_embedding = knowledge_embedding or embedding
        self.reranker = reranker or RerankerEngine(enabled=False)
        self.splitter = splitter or TextSplitter()

    @staticmethod
    def _rewrite_fts_query(query: str) -> str:
        """Rewrite a natural language query for FTS5.

        FTS5 uses implicit AND for space-separated terms, meaning every
        term must match. With natural language questions (e.g., "How does
        the auth middleware validate JWT tokens?"), this almost never
        matches any document because documents rarely contain all the
        exact words.

        This method converts NL queries to FTS5 OR syntax so that
        documents matching any significant term are returned, ranked
        by BM25 relevance. Stopwords are removed to reduce noise.

def _merge_duplicate_result(
        self,
        r: RetrievalResult,
        deduped: list[RetrievalResult],
    ) -> None:
        """Merge a duplicate result into the deduped list in place.

        If the existing entry is a "node" type, replace it with the
        specific-type version, preserving the higher relevance score.
        """
        for i, existing in enumerate(deduped):
            if existing.entity_id == r.entity_id and existing.entity_type == "node":
                if r.relevance_score < existing.relevance_score:
                    r = RetrievalResult(
                        entity_type=r.entity_type,
                        entity_id=r.entity_id,
                        text=r.text,
                        relevance_score=existing.relevance_score,
                        project=r.project,
                        subcategory=r.subcategory,
                        domain=r.domain,
                        semantic_score=r.semantic_score,
                        recency_score=r.recency_score,
                        importance_score=r.importance_score,
                        access_score=r.access_score,
                        graph_score=r.graph_score,
                        expansion_path=r.expansion_path,
                        hop_count=r.hop_count,
                        explanation=r.explanation,
                    )
                deduped[i] = r
                break

def test_held_out_cross_session_decision_recall(tmp_path: Path):
    """Cross-session: capture decisions, consolidate, retrieve in later session.

    Verifies that decisions captured in one session are persisted and
    retrievable after consolidation in a subsequent search/context call.
    """
    adapter = _setup_runtime(tmp_path)
    try:
        result = run_lifecycle_scenario("cross-session", adapter, mode="in_process")
        assert result.passed, f"Scenario failed: {result.errors}"
        assert len(result.tool_trace) > 0, "No operations were executed"
        # Scenario gates (not runner-added) must carry in_process provenance
        scenario_gates = [g for g in result.gates if g.execution_surface]
        for gate in scenario_gates:
            assert gate.execution_surface == "in_process", f"Gate {gate.name} has wrong surface: {gate.execution_surface}"
        # Capture persistence gate must have real numerator/denominator
        persistence = next(g for g in result.gates if g.name == "capture_persistence")
        assert persistence.numerator is not None, "Capture persistence gate has no numerator"
        assert persistence.denominator is not None, "Capture persistence gate has no denominator"
        # Consolidation must have completed without errors
        consolidation = next(g for g in result.gates if g.name == "consolidation_completed")
        assert consolidation.passed, "Consolidation failed"
    finally:
        adapter.state.close()

        """Rebuild fts_nodes FTS5 table if searchable_text or type column is missing.

        FTS5 virtual tables can't be ALTERed — must drop and recreate.
        """
        fts_cols = conn.execute("PRAGMA table_info(fts_nodes)").fetchall()
        fts_col_names = {row["name"] for row in fts_cols} if fts_cols else set()
        if "searchable_text" not in fts_col_names or "type" not in fts_col_names:
            conn.execute("DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS fts_nodes_ai")
            conn.execute("DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS fts_nodes_ad")
            conn.execute("DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS fts_nodes_au")
            conn.execute("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS fts_nodes")
            conn.execute(
                "CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE fts_nodes USING fts5("

def _delete_file(self, knowledge_type: str, title: str, fmt: str,
                     knowledge_id: str | None = None) -> None:
        """Remove the canonical file for a knowledge entry.

        If knowledge_id is provided, uses the new filename convention
        ({shortid}-{slug}.{ext}). Otherwise falls back to old format
        ({slug}.{ext}) for backward compatibility.
        """
        kdir = self._knowledge_dir(knowledge_type)
        if kdir is None:
            return
        ext = self.FILE_EXT.get(fmt, "md")
        if knowledge_id:
            filename = self.compute_filename(knowledge_id, title, fmt)
            path = kdir / filename
            if path.exists():
                path.unlink()
                return
            # Also check auto namespace
            auto_path = self._knowledge_dir(knowledge_type, auto=True)
            if auto_path:
                auto_file = auto_path / filename
                if auto_file.exists():
                    auto_file.unlink()
                    return
        else:
            # Old format fallback
            path = kdir / f"{self._safe_filename(title)}.{ext}"
            if path.exists():
                path.unlink()

def get_applied_migrations(self) -> list[str]:
        """Return the names of all applied schema migrations.

        Migrations are tracked in the ``schema_migrations`` table. The
        ``legacy_batch_v1`` entry represents all migrations that pre-date
        explicit tracking. Future migrations should be added with unique
        names via ``_record_migration_batch``.

        Returns:
            List of migration names in application order.
        """
        try:
            with self._connect() as conn:
                rows = conn.execute(
                    "SELECT name FROM schema_migrations ORDER BY id"
                ).fetchall()
            return [r["name"] for r in rows]
        except sqlite3.OperationalError:
            return []

sections.title: Storage
sections.content:
class Storage:
    """Primary SQLite storage for CogZ.

    Threading Contract
    ------------------
    Storage uses a **single persistent SQLite connection** (``self._conn``)
    with shared ``_in_transaction`` state.  This design is intentional:

    - SQLite WAL mode allows concurrent readers, but a single writer.
    - The persistent connection avoids per-request connection overhead.
    - Transaction nesting is tracked via ``_in_transaction`` to prevent
      nested BEGINs.

    **Consequence:** Storage instances are **NOT thread-safe**.  Concurrent
    access from multiple threads or interleaved async tasks will race on
    ``_in_transaction`` and connection state.

    **Mitigation:** The REST API uses ``SerializationMiddleware`` (see
    ``api.py``) to acquire an ``asyncio.Lock`` around every request,
    serializing all Storage access.  CLI and MCP server are single-threaded
    by design.  Any new entry point that touches Storage from multiple
    threads MUST acquire a lock before accessing the shared instance.

    The ``_connect()`` context manager yields the shared connection.
    Callers must not hold references to the connection outside the
    ``with`` block, as the connection may be closed and reopened between
    calls (health check in ``_get_conn``).
    """

    def __init__(self, db_path: Path | str, *, embedding_dim: int | None = None,
                 config_store: Any = None):
        """Initialize the Storage instance and ensure the database exists.

        Args:
            db_path: Path to the SQLite database file.
            embedding_dim: Optional override for the vec0 table dimension.
                If None, uses the EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS constant (default 384).
            config_store: Optional ConfigStore for config-aware checks
                (e.g., telemetry enablement). When None, only env vars
                control feature flags.

def run_code_context(adapter: BenchmarkAdapter, *, mode: str = "in_process", baseline: str = "full_cogz", seed: int = 42) -> BenchmarkResult:
    spec = SCENARIOS["code-context"]
    adapter = apply_baseline(adapter, baseline)
    result = _base_result(spec, mode, baseline, seed)
    env = _gate_env(result)
    trace = ToolTrace()
    try:
        responses: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
        for operation, kwargs in (
            ("index_repository", {"mode": "incremental"}),
            ("search", {"query": "cache", "top_k": 10}),
            ("get_context", {"query": "cache", "limit": 10}),
            ("build_context_pack", {"pack_type": "repository", "target": "fixture-repo"}),
        ):
            event = trace.record(operation, kwargs)
            response = getattr(adapter, operation)(**kwargs)
            event.finish(result=response)
            responses[operation] = response

        search_resp = responses.get("search", {})
        search_result_texts = _extract_result_texts(search_resp)
        index_resp = responses.get("index_repository", {})
        context_resp = responses.get("get_context", {})
        pack_resp = responses.get("build_context_pack", {})

        stats = index_resp.get("stats", {}) if isinstance(index_resp, dict) else {}
        search_result_ids = _extract_result_ids(search_resp)
        result.metrics["operations_completed"] = len(trace.events)
        result.metrics["indexed_files"] = stats.get("indexed", stats.get("files_indexed", stats.get("total", 0))) if isinstance(stats, dict) else 0
        result.metrics["search_results"] = len(search_result_ids)

        result.add_gate(gate_retrieval_recall(["cache"], search_result_texts, execution_surface=mode, seed=seed, environment=env))
        # nDCG: all search results for "cache" are relevant (indexed code
        # matching the query). The gate checks that results are returned

    spec = SCENARIOS["code-context"]
    adapter = apply_baseline(adapter, baseline)

    env = _gate_env(result)
    trace = ToolTrace()
    try:
        responses: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
        for operation, kwargs in (
            ("index_repository", {"mode": "incremental"}),
            ("search", {"query": "cache", "top_k": 10}),
            ("get_context", {"query": "cache", "limit": 10}),
            ("build_context_pack", {"pack_type": "repository", "target": "fixture-repo"}),
        ):
            event = trace.record(operation, kwargs)
            response = getattr(adapter, operation)(**kwargs)
            event.finish(result=response)
            responses[operation] = response

        search_resp = responses.get("search", {})
        search_result_texts = _extract_result_texts(search_resp)
        index_resp = responses.get("index_repository", {})
        context_resp = responses.get("get_context", {})

        and verifying model/dimension compatibility. Direct users to
        ``cogz maintenance reindex-embeddings`` for recovery.

        with self.storage._connect() as conn:

def test_held_out_cross_session_decision_recall(tmp_path: Path):
    """Cross-session: capture decisions, consolidate, retrieve in later session.

    Verifies that decisions captured in one session are persisted and
    retrievable after consolidation in a subsequent search/context call.
    """
    adapter = _setup_runtime(tmp_path)
    try:
        result = run_lifecycle_scenario("cross-session", adapter, mode="in_process")
        assert result.passed, f"Scenario failed: {result.errors}"
        assert len(result.tool_trace) > 0, "No operations were executed"
        # Scenario gates (not runner-added) must carry in_process provenance
        scenario_gates = [g for g in result.gates if g.execution_surface]
        for gate in scenario_gates:
            assert gate.execution_surface == "in_process", f"Gate {gate.name} has wrong surface: {gate.execution_surface}"
        # Capture persistence gate must have real numerator/denominator
        persistence = next(g for g in result.gates if g.name == "capture_persistence")
        assert persistence.numerator is not None, "Capture persistence gate has no numerator"
        assert persistence.denominator is not None, "Capture persistence gate has no denominator"
        # Consolidation must have completed without errors
        consolidation = next(g for g in result.gates if g.name == "consolidation_completed")
        assert consolidation.passed, "Consolidation failed"
    finally:
        adapter.state.close()

def test_generate_with_retry_async_does_not_block_event_loop(tmp_db):
    """Async retry uses asyncio.sleep, not time.sleep — event loop stays responsive."""
    call_count = 0

    class FlakyProvider(MockProvider):
        async def generate(self, prompt, **kwargs):
            nonlocal call_count
            call_count += 1
            if call_count < 3:
                exc = Exception("Service Unavailable")
                exc.status_code = 503
                raise exc
            return "Success after retry"

    config = ConfigStore()
    config.set_provider("mock")
    router = ModelRouter(config)
    router._provider = FlakyProvider()

    # Track whether a concurrent task runs during retry backoff
    concurrent_ran = []

    async def concurrent_task():
        # This should run during the retry backoff sleep
        await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
        concurrent_ran.append(True)

    async def main():
        # Start both tasks concurrently — if retry blocks the event loop,
        # concurrent_task won't complete until after the retry finishes
        with patch("cogz.model_router.LLM_RETRY_BASE_DELAY", 0.05):
            with patch("cogz.model_router.LLM_RETRY_MAX_DELAY", 0.1):
                retry_task = asyncio.create_task(
                    router.generate_with_retry("test", max_retries=3, operation="test")
                )
                conc_task = asyncio.create_task(concurrent_task())

def check_vector_coherence(self) -> CheckResult:
        """Check that stored text_hash matches re-derived hash for vectors.

        Phase 3.5: Re-derives text_hash from current content and compares
        to stored hash. Flags stale vectors (content changed without re-embedding).

        Not auto-fixable: re-embedding requires loading the embedding engine
        and verifying model/dimension compatibility. Direct users to
        ``cogz maintenance reindex-embeddings`` for recovery.
        """
        with self.storage._connect() as conn:
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='vec_entities'"

"""Search engine for CogZ (Phase 1B).

def test_held_out_constrained_runtime(tmp_path: Path):
    """Constrained runtime: exercise lifecycle with FTS-only search.

    Runs the lifecycle with FTS-only search (no embeddings), no reranking,
    and limited graph expansion. Verifies that the system degrades
    functionally without optional model dependencies.
    """
    adapter = _setup_runtime(tmp_path)
    try:
        result = run_lifecycle_scenario("constrained-runtime", adapter, mode="in_process")
        assert result.passed, f"Scenario failed: {result.errors}"
        assert len(result.tool_trace) > 0, "No operations were executed"
        scenario_gates = [g for g in result.gates if g.execution_surface]
        for gate in scenario_gates:
            assert gate.execution_surface == "in_process", f"Gate {gate.name} has wrong surface: {gate.execution_surface}"
        # Context must have content even in constrained mode
        context_gates = [g for g in result.gates if g.name == "context_has_content"]
        assert len(context_gates) >= 1, "No context_has_content gates found"
    finally:
        adapter.state.close()

def check_vector_coherence(self) -> CheckResult:
        """Check that stored text_hash matches re-derived hash for vectors.

        Phase 3.5: Re-derives text_hash from current content and compares
        to stored hash. Flags stale vectors (content changed without re-embedding).

        Not auto-fixable: re-embedding requires loading the embedding engine
        and verifying model/dimension compatibility. Direct users to
        ``cogz maintenance reindex-embeddings`` for recovery.
        """
        with self.storage._connect() as conn:
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='vec_entities'"
            ).fetchone()
        if not row:
            return CheckResult("vector_coherence", "skipped", {"reason": "No vec_entities table yet (Phase 1+)"})

        issues: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        with self.storage._connect() as conn:
            # Get all vectors with their stored text_hash
            vectors = conn.execute(
                "SELECT entity_type, entity_id, text_hash FROM vec_entities"
            ).fetchall()

            for entity_type, entity_id, stored_hash in vectors:
                if not stored_hash:
                    continue
                # Get current content for this entity
                content = self._get_entity_content(entity_type, entity_id)
                if content is None:
                    issues.append({
                        "entity_type": entity_type,
                        "entity_id": entity_id,
                        "issue": "entity_missing",
                        "severity": "error",
                    })
                    continue
                # Re-derive hash
                from .embedding import EmbeddingEngine
                rederived_hash = EmbeddingEngine._compute_hash(content)

    and limited graph expansion. Verifies that the system degrades

        context_gates = [g for g in result.gates if g.name == "context_has_content"]
        assert len(context_gates) >= 1, "No context_has_content gates found"

def test_generate_with_retry_async_does_not_block_event_loop(tmp_db):
    """Async retry uses asyncio.sleep, not time.sleep — event loop stays responsive."""
    call_count = 0

    class FlakyProvider(MockProvider):
        async def generate(self, prompt, **kwargs):
            nonlocal call_count
            call_count += 1
            if call_count < 3:
                exc = Exception("Service Unavailable")
                exc.status_code = 503
                raise exc
            return "Success after retry"

    config = ConfigStore()
    config.set_provider("mock")
    router = ModelRouter(config)
    router._provider = FlakyProvider()

    # Track whether a concurrent task runs during retry backoff
    concurrent_ran = []

    async def concurrent_task():
        # This should run during the retry backoff sleep
        await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
        concurrent_ran.append(True)

    async def main():
        # Start both tasks concurrently — if retry blocks the event loop,
        # concurrent_task won't complete until after the retry finishes
        with patch("cogz.model_router.LLM_RETRY_BASE_DELAY", 0.05):

                    router.generate_with_retry("test", max_retries=3, operation="test")

                conc_task = asyncio.create_task(concurrent_task())

def _clean_broken_cache() -> None:
    """Remove orphaned download artifacts that prevent model loading.

    huggingface_hub leaves ``.incomplete`` temp files when a download is
    interrupted and never garbage-collects them. A failed initial download
    can also leave ``refs/main`` empty (0 bytes), which causes
    ``snapshot_download(local_files_only=True)`` to return the ``snapshots/``
    parent dir instead of the hash subdir — onnxruntime then fails with
    NoSuchFile because ``snapshots/model.onnx`` doesn't exist. Both
    conditions block the model from ever loading and compound with each
    retry: every failed attempt adds another dead partial, filling the disk
    and making the next download fail even sooner.

    Safe with concurrent downloads: only ``.incomplete`` files older than
    ``_INCOMPLETE_STALE_SECONDS`` are removed (an active download keeps its
    file's mtime fresh). For empty ``refs/main``, only the file itself is
    deleted — not the model dir — so already-downloaded small files survive
    and ``snapshot_download`` raises ``LocalEntryNotFoundError`` (which
    fastembed catches and falls through to a network re-download).
    """
    cache = _get_hf_cache()
    if cache is None:
        return

    now = time.time()
    for f in cache.glob("models--*/blobs/*.incomplete"):
        try:
            if now - f.stat().st_mtime > _INCOMPLETE_STALE_SECONDS:
                f.unlink()
                logger.debug(f"Removed stale incomplete download: {f}")
        except OSError:
            pass

    for refs_main in cache.glob("models--*/refs/main"):
        try:
            if refs_main.stat().st_size == 0:
                refs_main.unlink()
                logger.warning(
                    f"Removed empty refs/main for "
                    f"{refs_main.parent.parent.name}"

sections.content:
class Storage:
    """Primary SQLite storage for CogZ.

    Threading Contract
    ------------------
    Storage uses a **single persistent SQLite connection** (``self._conn``)
    with shared ``_in_transaction`` state.  This design is intentional:

    - SQLite WAL mode allows concurrent readers, but a single writer.
    - The persistent connection avoids per-request connection overhead.
    - Transaction nesting is tracked via ``_in_transaction`` to prevent
      nested BEGINs.

    **Consequence:** Storage instances are **NOT thread-safe**.  Concurrent
    access from multiple threads or interleaved async tasks will race on
    ``_in_transaction`` and connection state.

    **Mitigation:** The REST API uses ``SerializationMiddleware`` (see
    ``api.py``) to acquire an ``asyncio.Lock`` around every request,
    serializing all Storage access.  CLI and MCP server are single-threaded
    by design.  Any new entry point that touches Storage from multiple
    threads MUST acquire a lock before accessing the shared instance.

    The ``_connect()`` context manager yields the shared connection.
    Callers must not hold references to the connection outside the
    ``with`` block, as the connection may be closed and reopened between
    calls (health check in ``_get_conn``).
    """

    def __init__(self, db_path: Path | str, *, embedding_dim: int | None = None,
                 config_store: Any = None):
        """Initialize the Storage instance and ensure the database exists.

        Args:
            db_path: Path to the SQLite database file.
            embedding_dim: Optional override for the vec0 table dimension.
                If None, uses the EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS constant (default 384).
            config_store: Optional ConfigStore for config-aware checks
                (e.g., telemetry enablement). When None, only env vars

def query_retrieval_log(
        self, entity_type: str | None = None, entity_id: str | None = None,
        limit: int = 100,
    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Query the retrieval log."""
        conditions: list[str] = []
        params: list[Any] = []
        if entity_type is not None:
            conditions.append("entity_type = ?")
            params.append(entity_type)
        if entity_id is not None:
            conditions.append("entity_id = ?")
            params.append(entity_id)
        where = " WHERE " + " AND ".join(conditions) if conditions else ""
        with self._connect() as conn:
            rows = conn.execute(
                f"SELECT * FROM retrieval_log{where} ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?",
                params + [limit],
            ).fetchall()
            return [dict(r) for r in rows]

def set_temporal_validity(
        self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str,
        valid_from: str | None = None, valid_until: str | None = None,
    ) -> bool:
        """Set temporal validity fields on a rule or knowledge entry."""
        table = entity_table(entity_type) if entity_type in ("rule", "knowledge") else None
        if table is None:
            return False
        parts: list[str] = []
        params: list[Any] = []
        if valid_from is not None:
            parts.append("valid_from = ?")
            params.append(valid_from)
        if valid_until is not None:
            parts.append("valid_until = ?")
            params.append(valid_until)
        if not parts:
            return False
        params.append(entity_id)
        with self._connect() as conn:
            cursor = conn.execute(
                f"UPDATE {table} SET {', '.join(parts)} WHERE id = ?",
                params,
            )
            if not self._in_transaction:
                conn.commit()
            return cursor.rowcount > 0

def _query(self, table: str, conditions: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        self._validate_table(table)
        with self._connect() as conn:
            sql = f"SELECT * FROM {table} WHERE 1=1"
            params: list[Any] = []
            if conditions:
                self._validate_columns(conditions)
                for k, v in conditions.items():
                    sql += f" AND {k} = ?"
                    params.append(v)
            rows = conn.execute(sql, params).fetchall()
            result = []
            for r in rows:

                self._deserialize_json_fields(d)

def query_telemetry(
        self,
        event_type: str | None = None,
        project_id: str | None = None,
        limit: int = 100,
    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Query telemetry events (newest first).

        Args:
            event_type: Optional event type filter.
            project_id: Optional project filter.
            limit: Maximum results (default 100).

        Returns:
            List of telemetry dicts with deserialized payloads.
        """
        with self._connect() as conn:
            sql = "SELECT * FROM telemetry WHERE 1=1"
            params: list[Any] = []
            if event_type:
                sql += " AND event_type = ?"
                params.append(event_type)
            if project_id:
                sql += " AND project_id = ?"
                params.append(project_id)
            sql += " ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?"
            params.append(limit)
            rows = conn.execute(sql, params).fetchall()
            result = []
            for r in rows:
                d = dict(r)
                try:
                    d["payload"] = json.loads(d["payload"])
                except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
                    pass
                result.append(d)
            return result

            # Also check auto namespace
            auto_path = self._knowledge_dir(knowledge_type, auto=True)
            if auto_path:
                auto_file = auto_path / filename
                if auto_file.exists():
                    auto_file.unlink()
                    return
        else:
            # Old format fallback
            path = kdir / f"{self._safe_filename(title)}.{ext}"
            if path.exists():
                path.unlink()

def delete(self, knowledge_id: str, force: bool = False) -> bool:
        """Delete a knowledge entry by ID.

        Args:
            knowledge_id: The knowledge entry ID.
            force: If True, bypass protection checks (consolidation_locked,
                high importance). Use with caution.

        Returns:
            True if the deletion succeeded, False otherwise.
        """
        if not force:
            entry = self.get(knowledge_id)
            if entry and self._is_protected(knowledge_id):
                raise ProtectedEntryError(
                    f"Knowledge entry {knowledge_id} is protected "
                    "(consolidation_locked or high importance). Use force=True to override."
                )
        entry = self.get(knowledge_id)
        # Delete DB record first — if this fails, the file remains on disk
        # and can be cleaned up on retry. If file deletion fails after DB
        # delete, sync_from_files will detect the orphaned DB record.
        deleted = self.storage._delete("knowledge", knowledge_id)
        if deleted and self.repo_path is not None and entry:
            try:
                self._delete_file(
                    entry.get("type", "knowledge"),
                    entry.get("title", ""),
                    entry.get("format", "markdown"),
                    knowledge_id=knowledge_id,
                )
            except OSError as exc:
                logger.warning(f"DB record deleted but file removal failed for {knowledge_id}: {exc}")
            self.storage.record_event(
                "KnowledgeDeleted",
                {"entity_id": knowledge_id},
                project_id=entry.get("project") if entry else None,
            )
        return deleted

def _clean_broken_cache() -> None:
    """Remove orphaned download artifacts that prevent model loading.

    huggingface_hub leaves ``.incomplete`` temp files when a download is
    interrupted and never garbage-collects them. A failed initial download
    can also leave ``refs/main`` empty (0 bytes), which causes
    ``snapshot_download(local_files_only=True)`` to return the ``snapshots/``
    parent dir instead of the hash subdir — onnxruntime then fails with
    NoSuchFile because ``snapshots/model.onnx`` doesn't exist. Both
    conditions block the model from ever loading and compound with each
    retry: every failed attempt adds another dead partial, filling the disk
    and making the next download fail even sooner.

    Safe with concurrent downloads: only ``.incomplete`` files older than
    ``_INCOMPLETE_STALE_SECONDS`` are removed (an active download keeps its
    file's mtime fresh). For empty ``refs/main``, only the file itself is
    deleted — not the model dir — so already-downloaded small files survive
    and ``snapshot_download`` raises ``LocalEntryNotFoundError`` (which
    fastembed catches and falls through to a network re-download).
    """
    cache = _get_hf_cache()
    if cache is None:
        return

    now = time.time()
    for f in cache.glob("models--*/blobs/*.incomplete"):
        try:
            if now - f.stat().st_mtime > _INCOMPLETE_STALE_SECONDS:
                f.unlink()
                logger.debug(f"Removed stale incomplete download: {f}")
        except OSError:
            pass

    for refs_main in cache.glob("models--*/refs/main"):
        try:
            if refs_main.stat().st_size == 0:
                refs_main.unlink()
                logger.warning(
                    f"Removed empty refs/main for "
                    f"{refs_main.parent.parent.name}"

class Storage:
    """Primary SQLite storage for CogZ.

    Threading Contract
    ------------------
    Storage uses a **single persistent SQLite connection** (``self._conn``)
    with shared ``_in_transaction`` state.  This design is intentional:

    - SQLite WAL mode allows concurrent readers, but a single writer.
    - The persistent connection avoids per-request connection overhead.
    - Transaction nesting is tracked via ``_in_transaction`` to prevent
      nested BEGINs.

    **Consequence:** Storage instances are **NOT thread-safe**.  Concurrent
    access from multiple threads or interleaved async tasks will race on
    ``_in_transaction`` and connection state.

    **Mitigation:** The REST API uses ``SerializationMiddleware`` (see
    ``api.py``) to acquire an ``asyncio.Lock`` around every request,
    serializing all Storage access.  CLI and MCP server are single-threaded
    by design.  Any new entry point that touches Storage from multiple
    threads MUST acquire a lock before accessing the shared instance.

    The ``_connect()`` context manager yields the shared connection.
    Callers must not hold references to the connection outside the
    ``with`` block, as the connection may be closed and reopened between
    calls (health check in ``_get_conn``).
    """

    def __init__(self, db_path: Path | str, *, embedding_dim: int | None = None,
                 config_store: Any = None):
        """Initialize the Storage instance and ensure the database exists.

        Args:
            db_path: Path to the SQLite database file.
            embedding_dim: Optional override for the vec0 table dimension.
                If None, uses the EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS constant (default 384).
            config_store: Optional ConfigStore for config-aware checks
                (e.g., telemetry enablement). When None, only env vars
                control feature flags.

        self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str,
        valid_from: str | None = None, valid_until: str | None = None,
    ) -> bool:
        """Set temporal validity fields on a rule or knowledge entry."""
        table = entity_table(entity_type) if entity_type in ("rule", "knowledge") else None
        if table is None:
            return False
        parts: list[str] = []
        params: list[Any] = []
        if valid_from is not None:
            parts.append("valid_from = ?")
            params.append(valid_from)
        if valid_until is not None:
            parts.append("valid_until = ?")
            params.append(valid_until)
        if not parts:
            return False
        params.append(entity_id)
        with self._connect() as conn:
            cursor = conn.execute(
                f"UPDATE {table} SET {', '.join(parts)} WHERE id = ?",
                params,
            )
            if not self._in_transaction:
                conn.commit()
            return cursor.rowcount > 0

def _fetch_entities_for_reindex(
        self,
        storage: Any,
        etype: str,
        spec: EntitySpec,
        project: str | None,
    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Fetch entities from storage for reindexing.

        For "node" entity type with code model, filters to only code node
        types (Function, Class, File, etc.). Knowledge entries stored as
        nodes are excluded — they have their own table entries with bge-base
        embeddings. Also fetches consolidation_status for vec_entities sync.
        """
        from .constants import CODE_ENTITY_TYPES, CODE_NODE_TYPES

        is_code = etype in CODE_ENTITY_TYPES
        table = spec.table
        text_expr = spec.text_expr
        proj_col = spec.project_col

        with storage._connect() as conn:
            status_expr = "consolidation_status" if "consolidation_status" in [
                row["name"] for row in conn.execute(f"PRAGMA table_info({table})").fetchall()
            ] else "'active' as consolidation_status"
            if etype == "node" and is_code:
                placeholders = ", ".join(["?"] * len(CODE_NODE_TYPES))
                sql = f"SELECT id, {text_expr} as text, {proj_col} as project, subcategory, domain, {status_expr} FROM {table} WHERE type IN ({placeholders})"
                params: list[Any] = list(CODE_NODE_TYPES)
                if project:
                    sql += f" AND {proj_col} = ?"
                    params.append(project)
            else:
                sql = f"SELECT id, {text_expr} as text, {proj_col} as project, subcategory, domain, {status_expr} FROM {table}"
                params = []
                if project:
                    sql += f" WHERE {proj_col} = ?"
                    params.append(project)
            rows = conn.execute(sql, params).fetchall()
            return [dict(r) for r in rows if r["text"]]

def _clean_broken_cache() -> None:
    """Remove orphaned download artifacts that prevent model loading.

    huggingface_hub leaves ``.incomplete`` temp files when a download is
    interrupted and never garbage-collects them. A failed initial download
    can also leave ``refs/main`` empty (0 bytes), which causes
    ``snapshot_download(local_files_only=True)`` to return the ``snapshots/``
    parent dir instead of the hash subdir — onnxruntime then fails with
    NoSuchFile because ``snapshots/model.onnx`` doesn't exist. Both
    conditions block the model from ever loading and compound with each
    retry: every failed attempt adds another dead partial, filling the disk
    and making the next download fail even sooner.

    Safe with concurrent downloads: only ``.incomplete`` files older than
    ``_INCOMPLETE_STALE_SECONDS`` are removed (an active download keeps its
    file's mtime fresh). For empty ``refs/main``, only the file itself is
    deleted — not the model dir — so already-downloaded small files survive
    and ``snapshot_download`` raises ``LocalEntryNotFoundError`` (which
    fastembed catches and falls through to a network re-download).
    """
    cache = _get_hf_cache()
    if cache is None:
        return

    now = time.time()
    for f in cache.glob("models--*/blobs/*.incomplete"):
        try:
            if now - f.stat().st_mtime > _INCOMPLETE_STALE_SECONDS:
                f.unlink()
                logger.debug(f"Removed stale incomplete download: {f}")
        except OSError:
            pass

    for refs_main in cache.glob("models--*/refs/main"):
        try:
            if refs_main.stat().st_size == 0:
                refs_main.unlink()
                logger.warning(
                    f"Removed empty refs/main for "
                    f"{refs_main.parent.parent.name}"

sections.title: Storage
sections.content:
class Storage:
    """Primary SQLite storage for CogZ.

    Threading Contract
    ------------------
    Storage uses a **single persistent SQLite connection** (``self._conn``)
    with shared ``_in_transaction`` state.  This design is intentional:

    - SQLite WAL mode allows concurrent readers, but a single writer.
    - The persistent connection avoids per-request connection overhead.
    - Transaction nesting is tracked via ``_in_transaction`` to prevent
      nested BEGINs.

    **Consequence:** Storage instances are **NOT thread-safe**.  Concurrent
    access from multiple threads or interleaved async tasks will race on
    ``_in_transaction`` and connection state.

    **Mitigation:** The REST API uses ``SerializationMiddleware`` (see
    ``api.py``) to acquire an ``asyncio.Lock`` around every request,
    serializing all Storage access.  CLI and MCP server are single-threaded
    by design.  Any new entry point that touches Storage from multiple
    threads MUST acquire a lock before accessing the shared instance.

    The ``_connect()`` context manager yields the shared connection.
    Callers must not hold references to the connection outside the
    ``with`` block, as the connection may be closed and reopened between
    calls (health check in ``_get_conn``).
    """

    def __init__(self, db_path: Path | str, *, embedding_dim: int | None = None,
                 config_store: Any = None):
        """Initialize the Storage instance and ensure the database exists.

        Args:
            db_path: Path to the SQLite database file.
            embedding_dim: Optional override for the vec0 table dimension.
                If None, uses the EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS constant (default 384).
            config_store: Optional ConfigStore for config-aware checks
                (e.g., telemetry enablement). When None, only env vars
                control feature flags.

def query_retrieval_log(
        self, entity_type: str | None = None, entity_id: str | None = None,
        limit: int = 100,
    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Query the retrieval log."""
        conditions: list[str] = []
        params: list[Any] = []
        if entity_type is not None:
            conditions.append("entity_type = ?")
            params.append(entity_type)
        if entity_id is not None:
            conditions.append("entity_id = ?")
            params.append(entity_id)
        where = " WHERE " + " AND ".join(conditions) if conditions else ""
        with self._connect() as conn:
            rows = conn.execute(
                f"SELECT * FROM retrieval_log{where} ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?",
                params + [limit],
            ).fetchall()
            return [dict(r) for r in rows]

def set_temporal_validity(
        self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str,
        valid_from: str | None = None, valid_until: str | None = None,
    ) -> bool:
        """Set temporal validity fields on a rule or knowledge entry."""
        table = entity_table(entity_type) if entity_type in ("rule", "knowledge") else None
        if table is None:
            return False
        parts: list[str] = []
        params: list[Any] = []
        if valid_from is not None:
            parts.append("valid_from = ?")
            params.append(valid_from)
        if valid_until is not None:
            parts.append("valid_until = ?")
            params.append(valid_until)
        if not parts:
            return False
        params.append(entity_id)
        with self._connect() as conn:
            cursor = conn.execute(
                f"UPDATE {table} SET {', '.join(parts)} WHERE id = ?",
                params,
            )
            if not self._in_transaction:
                conn.commit()
            return cursor.rowcount > 0

def _query(self, table: str, conditions: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        self._validate_table(table)
        with self._connect() as conn:
            sql = f"SELECT * FROM {table} WHERE 1=1"
            params: list[Any] = []
            if conditions:
                self._validate_columns(conditions)
                for k, v in conditions.items():
                    sql += f" AND {k} = ?"
                    params.append(v)
            rows = conn.execute(sql, params).fetchall()
            result = []
            for r in rows:
                d = dict(r)
                self._deserialize_json_fields(d)
                result.append(d)
            return result

def _clean_broken_cache() -> None:
    """Remove orphaned download artifacts that prevent model loading.

    huggingface_hub leaves ``.incomplete`` temp files when a download is
    interrupted and never garbage-collects them. A failed initial download
    can also leave ``refs/main`` empty (0 bytes), which causes
    ``snapshot_download(local_files_only=True)`` to return the ``snapshots/``
    parent dir instead of the hash subdir — onnxruntime then fails with
    NoSuchFile because ``snapshots/model.onnx`` doesn't exist. Both
    conditions block the model from ever loading and compound with each
    retry: every failed attempt adds another dead partial, filling the disk
    and making the next download fail even sooner.

    Safe with concurrent downloads: only ``.incomplete`` files older than
    ``_INCOMPLETE_STALE_SECONDS`` are removed (an active download keeps its
    file's mtime fresh). For empty ``refs/main``, only the file itself is
    deleted — not the model dir — so already-downloaded small files survive
    and ``snapshot_download`` raises ``LocalEntryNotFoundError`` (which
    fastembed catches and falls through to a network re-download).
    """
    cache = _get_hf_cache()
    if cache is None:
        return

    now = time.time()
    for f in cache.glob("models--*/blobs/*.incomplete"):
        try:
            if now - f.stat().st_mtime > _INCOMPLETE_STALE_SECONDS:
                f.unlink()
                logger.debug(f"Removed stale incomplete download: {f}")
        except OSError:
            pass

    for refs_main in cache.glob("models--*/refs/main"):
        try:
            if refs_main.stat().st_size == 0:
                refs_main.unlink()
                logger.warning(
                    f"Removed empty refs/main for "
                    f"{refs_main.parent.parent.name}"

class Storage:
    """Primary SQLite storage for CogZ.

    Threading Contract
    ------------------
    Storage uses a **single persistent SQLite connection** (``self._conn``)
    with shared ``_in_transaction`` state.  This design is intentional:

    - SQLite WAL mode allows concurrent readers, but a single writer.
    - The persistent connection avoids per-request connection overhead.
    - Transaction nesting is tracked via ``_in_transaction`` to prevent
      nested BEGINs.

    **Consequence:** Storage instances are **NOT thread-safe**.  Concurrent
    access from multiple threads or interleaved async tasks will race on
    ``_in_transaction`` and connection state.

    **Mitigation:** The REST API uses ``SerializationMiddleware`` (see
    ``api.py``) to acquire an ``asyncio.Lock`` around every request,
    serializing all Storage access.  CLI and MCP server are single-threaded
    by design.  Any new entry point that touches Storage from multiple
    threads MUST acquire a lock before accessing the shared instance.

    The ``_connect()`` context manager yields the shared connection.
    Callers must not hold references to the connection outside the
    ``with`` block, as the connection may be closed and reopened between
    calls (health check in ``_get_conn``).
    """

    def __init__(self, db_path: Path | str, *, embedding_dim: int | None = None,
                 config_store: Any = None):
        """Initialize the Storage instance and ensure the database exists.

        Args:
            db_path: Path to the SQLite database file.
            embedding_dim: Optional override for the vec0 table dimension.
                If None, uses the EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS constant (default 384).
            config_store: Optional ConfigStore for config-aware checks
                (e.g., telemetry enablement). When None, only env vars
                control feature flags.

def query_retrieval_log(
        self, entity_type: str | None = None, entity_id: str | None = None,
        limit: int = 100,
    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Query the retrieval log."""
        conditions: list[str] = []
        params: list[Any] = []
        if entity_type is not None:
            conditions.append("entity_type = ?")
            params.append(entity_type)
        if entity_id is not None:
            conditions.append("entity_id = ?")
            params.append(entity_id)
        where = " WHERE " + " AND ".join(conditions) if conditions else ""
        with self._connect() as conn:
            rows = conn.execute(
                f"SELECT * FROM retrieval_log{where} ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?",
                params + [limit],
            ).fetchall()
            return [dict(r) for r in rows]

def set_temporal_validity(
        self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str,
        valid_from: str | None = None, valid_until: str | None = None,
    ) -> bool:
        """Set temporal validity fields on a rule or knowledge entry."""
        table = entity_table(entity_type) if entity_type in ("rule", "knowledge") else None
        if table is None:
            return False
        parts: list[str] = []
        params: list[Any] = []
        if valid_from is not None:
            parts.append("valid_from = ?")
            params.append(valid_from)
        if valid_until is not None:
            parts.append("valid_until = ?")
            params.append(valid_until)
        if not parts:
            return False
        params.append(entity_id)
        with self._connect() as conn:
            cursor = conn.execute(
                f"UPDATE {table} SET {', '.join(parts)} WHERE id = ?",
                params,
            )
            if not self._in_transaction:
                conn.commit()
            return cursor.rowcount > 0

sections.content:
def _clean_broken_cache() -> None:
    """Remove orphaned download artifacts that prevent model loading.

    huggingface_hub leaves ``.incomplete`` temp files when a download is
    interrupted and never garbage-collects them. A failed initial download
    can also leave ``refs/main`` empty (0 bytes), which causes
    ``snapshot_download(local_files_only=True)`` to return the ``snapshots/``
    parent dir instead of the hash subdir — onnxruntime then fails with
    NoSuchFile because ``snapshots/model.onnx`` doesn't exist. Both
    conditions block the model from ever loading and compound with each
    retry: every failed attempt adds another dead partial, filling the disk
    and making the next download fail even sooner.

    Safe with concurrent downloads: only ``.incomplete`` files older than
    ``_INCOMPLETE_STALE_SECONDS`` are removed (an active download keeps its
    file's mtime fresh). For empty ``refs/main``, only the file itself is
    deleted — not the model dir — so already-downloaded small files survive
    and ``snapshot_download`` raises ``LocalEntryNotFoundError`` (which
    fastembed catches and falls through to a network re-download).
    """
    cache = _get_hf_cache()
    if cache is None:
        return

    now = time.time()
    for f in cache.glob("models--*/blobs/*.incomplete"):
        try:
            if now - f.stat().st_mtime > _INCOMPLETE_STALE_SECONDS:
                f.unlink()
                logger.debug(f"Removed stale incomplete download: {f}")
        except OSError:
            pass

    for refs_main in cache.glob("models--*/refs/main"):
        try:
            if refs_main.stat().st_size == 0:
                refs_main.unlink()
                logger.warning(
                    f"Removed empty refs/main for "
                    f"{refs_main.parent.parent.name}"

    """Constrained runtime: exercise lifecycle with FTS-only search.

    Runs the lifecycle with FTS-only search (no embeddings), no reranking,

        assert len(result.tool_trace) > 0, "No operations were executed"
        scenario_gates = [g for g in result.gates if g.execution_surface]
        for gate in scenario_gates:
            assert gate.execution_surface == "in_process", f"Gate {gate.name} has wrong surface: {gate.execution_surface}"
        # Context must have content even in constrained mode
        context_gates = [g for g in result.gates if g.name == "context_has_content"]

class Storage:
    """Primary SQLite storage for CogZ.

    Threading Contract
    ------------------
    Storage uses a **single persistent SQLite connection** (``self._conn``)
    with shared ``_in_transaction`` state.  This design is intentional:

    - SQLite WAL mode allows concurrent readers, but a single writer.
    - The persistent connection avoids per-request connection overhead.
    - Transaction nesting is tracked via ``_in_transaction`` to prevent
      nested BEGINs.

    **Consequence:** Storage instances are **NOT thread-safe**.  Concurrent
    access from multiple threads or interleaved async tasks will race on
    ``_in_transaction`` and connection state.

    **Mitigation:** The REST API uses ``SerializationMiddleware`` (see
    ``api.py``) to acquire an ``asyncio.Lock`` around every request,
    serializing all Storage access.  CLI and MCP server are single-threaded
    by design.  Any new entry point that touches Storage from multiple
    threads MUST acquire a lock before accessing the shared instance.

    The ``_connect()`` context manager yields the shared connection.
    Callers must not hold references to the connection outside the
    ``with`` block, as the connection may be closed and reopened between
    calls (health check in ``_get_conn``).
    """

    def __init__(self, db_path: Path | str, *, embedding_dim: int | None = None,
                 config_store: Any = None):

            db_path: Path to the SQLite database file.

                If None, uses the EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS constant (default 384).
            config_store: Optional ConfigStore for config-aware checks
                (e.g., telemetry enablement). When None, only env vars
                control feature flags.

        self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str,
        valid_from: str | None = None, valid_until: str | None = None,
    ) -> bool:
        """Set temporal validity fields on a rule or knowledge entry."""
        table = entity_table(entity_type) if entity_type in ("rule", "knowledge") else None
        if table is None:
            return False
        parts: list[str] = []
        params: list[Any] = []
        if valid_from is not None:
            parts.append("valid_from = ?")
            params.append(valid_from)
        if valid_until is not None:
            parts.append("valid_until = ?")
            params.append(valid_until)
        if not parts:
            return False
        params.append(entity_id)
        with self._connect() as conn:
            cursor = conn.execute(
                f"UPDATE {table} SET {', '.join(parts)} WHERE id = ?",
                params,
            )
            if not self._in_transaction:
                conn.commit()
            return cursor.rowcount > 0

def _fetch_entities_for_reindex(
        self,
        storage: Any,
        etype: str,
        spec: EntitySpec,
        project: str | None,
    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Fetch entities from storage for reindexing.

        For "node" entity type with code model, filters to only code node
        types (Function, Class, File, etc.). Knowledge entries stored as
        nodes are excluded — they have their own table entries with bge-base
        embeddings. Also fetches consolidation_status for vec_entities sync.
        """
        from .constants import CODE_ENTITY_TYPES, CODE_NODE_TYPES

        is_code = etype in CODE_ENTITY_TYPES
        table = spec.table
        text_expr = spec.text_expr
        proj_col = spec.project_col

        with storage._connect() as conn:
            status_expr = "consolidation_status" if "consolidation_status" in [
                row["name"] for row in conn.execute(f"PRAGMA table_info({table})").fetchall()
            ] else "'active' as consolidation_status"
            if etype == "node" and is_code:
                placeholders = ", ".join(["?"] * len(CODE_NODE_TYPES))
                sql = f"SELECT id, {text_expr} as text, {proj_col} as project, subcategory, domain, {status_expr} FROM {table} WHERE type IN ({placeholders})"
                params: list[Any] = list(CODE_NODE_TYPES)
                if project:
                    sql += f" AND {proj_col} = ?"
                    params.append(project)
            else:
                sql = f"SELECT id, {text_expr} as text, {proj_col} as project, subcategory, domain, {status_expr} FROM {table}"
                params = []
                if project:
                    sql += f" WHERE {proj_col} = ?"
                    params.append(project)
            rows = conn.execute(sql, params).fetchall()
            return [dict(r) for r in rows if r["text"]]
