def _clean_broken_cache() -> None:
    """Remove orphaned download artifacts that prevent model loading.

    huggingface_hub leaves ``.incomplete`` temp files when a download is
    interrupted and never garbage-collects them. A failed initial download
    can also leave ``refs/main`` empty (0 bytes), which causes
    ``snapshot_download(local_files_only=True)`` to return the ``snapshots/``
    parent dir instead of the hash subdir — onnxruntime then fails with
    NoSuchFile because ``snapshots/model.onnx`` doesn't exist. Both
    conditions block the model from ever loading and compound with each
    retry: every failed attempt adds another dead partial, filling the disk
    and making the next download fail even sooner.

    Safe with concurrent downloads: only ``.incomplete`` files older than
    ``_INCOMPLETE_STALE_SECONDS`` are removed (an active download keeps its
    file's mtime fresh). For empty ``refs/main``, only the file itself is
    deleted — not the model dir — so already-downloaded small files survive
    and ``snapshot_download`` raises ``LocalEntryNotFoundError`` (which
    fastembed catches and falls through to a network re-download).
    """
    cache = _get_hf_cache()
    if cache is None:
        return

    now = time.time()
    for f in cache.glob("models--*/blobs/*.incomplete"):
        try:
            if now - f.stat().st_mtime > _INCOMPLETE_STALE_SECONDS:
                f.unlink()
                logger.debug(f"Removed stale incomplete download: {f}")
        except OSError:
            pass

    for refs_main in cache.glob("models--*/refs/main"):
        try:
            if refs_main.stat().st_size == 0:
                refs_main.unlink()
                logger.warning(
                    f"Removed empty refs/main for "
                    f"{refs_main.parent.parent.name}"

def _delete_file(self, knowledge_type: str, title: str, fmt: str,
                     knowledge_id: str | None = None) -> None:
        """Remove the canonical file for a knowledge entry.

        If knowledge_id is provided, uses the new filename convention
        ({shortid}-{slug}.{ext}). Otherwise falls back to old format
        ({slug}.{ext}) for backward compatibility.
        """
        kdir = self._knowledge_dir(knowledge_type)
        if kdir is None:
            return
        ext = self.FILE_EXT.get(fmt, "md")
        if knowledge_id:
            filename = self.compute_filename(knowledge_id, title, fmt)
            path = kdir / filename
            if path.exists():
                path.unlink()
                return
            # Also check auto namespace
            auto_path = self._knowledge_dir(knowledge_type, auto=True)
            if auto_path:
                auto_file = auto_path / filename
                if auto_file.exists():
                    auto_file.unlink()
                    return
        else:
            # Old format fallback
            path = kdir / f"{self._safe_filename(title)}.{ext}"
            if path.exists():
                path.unlink()

def test_held_out_code_context_localization(tmp_path: Path):
    """Code-context: index a repository and retrieve code context.

    Indexes a repository with a Python file containing a cache implementation,
    then searches for code context and builds a context pack.
    """
    adapter = _setup_runtime(tmp_path)
    try:
        result = run_lifecycle_scenario("code-context", adapter, mode="in_process")
        assert result.passed, f"Scenario failed: {result.errors}"
        assert len(result.tool_trace) > 0, "No operations were executed"
        scenario_gates = [g for g in result.gates if g.execution_surface]
        for gate in scenario_gates:
            assert gate.execution_surface == "in_process", f"Gate {gate.name} has wrong surface: {gate.execution_surface}"
        # Retrieval recall gate must have real data
        recall = next(g for g in result.gates if g.name == "retrieval_recall")
        assert recall.numerator is not None, "Retrieval recall gate has no numerator"
        # Index must have indexed files
        assert result.metrics.get("indexed_files", 0) > 0, "No files were indexed"
    finally:
        adapter.state.close()

def run_python(code, timeout=60):
    """Run inline Python code with cogz on PYTHONPATH."""
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["PYTHONPATH"] = str(COGZ_REPO / "src")
    result = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", code],
                            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout, env=env)
    return result.returncode, result.stdout.strip(), result.stderr.strip()

def delete_node(self, node_id: str) -> bool:
        """Delete a node by its unique identifier.

        Args:
            node_id: The unique identifier of the node to delete.

def _clean_broken_cache() -> None:
    """Remove orphaned download artifacts that prevent model loading.

    huggingface_hub leaves ``.incomplete`` temp files when a download is
    interrupted and never garbage-collects them. A failed initial download
    can also leave ``refs/main`` empty (0 bytes), which causes
    ``snapshot_download(local_files_only=True)`` to return the ``snapshots/``
    parent dir instead of the hash subdir — onnxruntime then fails with
    NoSuchFile because ``snapshots/model.onnx`` doesn't exist. Both
    conditions block the model from ever loading and compound with each
    retry: every failed attempt adds another dead partial, filling the disk
    and making the next download fail even sooner.

    Safe with concurrent downloads: only ``.incomplete`` files older than
    ``_INCOMPLETE_STALE_SECONDS`` are removed (an active download keeps its
    file's mtime fresh). For empty ``refs/main``, only the file itself is
    deleted — not the model dir — so already-downloaded small files survive
    and ``snapshot_download`` raises ``LocalEntryNotFoundError`` (which
    fastembed catches and falls through to a network re-do...

def clear_nodes_by_types(self, node_types: set[str]) -> dict[str, int]:
        """Bulk-delete nodes of the given types and all edges connected to them.

        Also cleans up stale vectors from ``vec_entities`` for the deleted
        node IDs, preventing ``entity_missing`` warnings in doctor checks
        after a full re-index.

        Args:
            node_types: Set of node type strings to remove.

        Returns:
            dict with 'nodes_deleted' and 'edges_deleted' counts.
        """
        if not node_types:
            return {"nodes_deleted": 0, "edges_deleted": 0}
        placeholders = ",".join("?" for _ in node_types)
        with self._connect() as conn:
            # Clean up stale vectors for nodes about to be deleted
            # (must run before node deletion — vec_entities has no FK to nodes)
            try:
                conn.execute(
                    f"""DELETE FROM vec_entities WHERE entity_id IN (
                        SELECT id FROM nodes WHERE type IN ({placeholders})
                    )""",
                    list(node_types),
                )
            except Exception as exc:

def _index_corpus(
    state: Any,
    dataset: RetrievalDataset,
    progress_every: int = 500,
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Index corpus documents into CogZ storage as observations.

    Stores the original corpus doc_id in observation properties so we can
    map search results back.

    Returns:
        Dict mapping CogZ entity_id → corpus doc_id.
    """
    entity_to_doc: dict[str, str] = {}
    learning = state.learning

    for i, (doc_id, text, title) in enumerate(dataset.corpus):
        # Combine title + text for indexing (title is often empty for code)
        statement = f"{title}\n{text}" if title else text
        if not statement.strip():
            statement = f"[empty doc {doc_id}]"

        # Use doc_id as source to prevent dedup and enable mapping
        obs_id = learning.create_observation(
            statement=statement[:10000],  # truncate very long docs
            source=f"benchmark:{doc_id}",
            category="BENCHMARK",
            project=BENCHMARK_PROJECT,
            subcategory=BENCHMARK_SUBCATEGORY,
            domain=BENCHMARK_DOMAIN,
            properties={"benchmark_doc_id": doc_id},
        )
        entity_to_doc[obs_id] = doc_id

        if (i + 1) % progress_every == 0:
            logger.info(f"  Indexed {i + 1}/{dataset.num_corpus} docs...")

    return entity_to_doc

def _clean_broken_cache() -> None:
    """Remove orphaned download artifacts that prevent model loading.

    huggingface_hub leaves ``.incomplete`` temp files when a download is
    interrupted and never garbage-collects them. A failed initial download
    can also leave ``refs/main`` empty (0 bytes), which causes
    ``snapshot_download(local_files_only=True)`` to return the ``snapshots/``
    parent dir instead of the hash subdir — onnxruntime then fails with
    NoSuchFile because ``snapshots/model.onnx`` doesn't exist. Both
    conditions block the model from ever loading and compound with each
    retry: every failed attempt adds another dead partial, filling the disk
    and making the next download fail even sooner.

    Safe with concurrent downloads: only ``.incomplete`` files older than
    ``_INCOMPLETE_STALE_SECONDS`` are removed (an active download keeps its
    file's mtime fresh). For empty ``refs/main``, only the file itself is
    deleted — not the model dir — so already-downloaded small files survive
    and ``snapshot_download`` raises ``LocalEntryNotFoundError`` (which
    fastembed catches and falls through to a network re-download).
    """
    cache = _get_hf_cache()
    if cache is None:
        return

    now = time.time()
    for f in cache.glob("models--*/blobs/*.incomplete"):
        try:
            if now - f.stat().st_mtime > _INCOMPLETE_STALE_SECONDS:
                f.unlink()
                logger.debug(f"Removed stale incomplete download: {f}")
        except OSError:
            pass

    for refs_main in cache.glob("models--*/refs/main"):
        try:
            if refs_main.stat().st_size == 0:
                refs_main.unlink()
                logger.warning(
                    f"Removed empty refs/main for "
                    f"{refs_main.parent.parent.name}"

    """Code-context: index a repository and retrieve code context.

    Indexes a repository with a Python file containing a cache implementation,
    then searches for code context and builds a context pack.

        assert result.passed, f"Scenario failed: {result.errors}"
        assert len(result.tool_trace) > 0, "No operations were executed"
        scenario_gates = [g for g in result.gates if g.execution_surface]
        for gate in scenario_gates:
            assert gate.execution_surface == "in_process", f"Gate {gate.name} has wrong surface: {gate.execution_surface}"
        # Retrieval recall gate must have real data
        recall = next(g for g in result.gates if g.name == "retrieval_recall")
        assert recall.numerator is not None, "Retrieval recall gate has no numerator"
        # Index must have indexed files
        assert result.metrics.get("indexed_files", 0) > 0, "No files were indexed"
    finally:

            result = cursor.rowcount > 0
        if result:

sections.title: _clean_broken_cache
sections.content:
def _clean_broken_cache() -> None:
    """Remove orphaned download artifacts that prevent model loading.

    huggingface_hub leaves ``.incomplete`` temp files when a download is
    interrupted and never garbage-collects them. A failed initial download
    can also leave ``refs/main`` empty (0 bytes), which causes
    ``snapshot_download(local_files_only=True)`` to return the ``snapshots/``
    parent dir instead of the hash subdir — onnxruntime then fails with
    NoSuchFile because ``snapshots/model.onnx`` doesn't exist. Both
    conditions block the model from ever loading and compound with each
    retry: every failed attempt adds another dead partial, filling the disk
    and making the next download fail even sooner.

    Safe with concurrent downloads: only ``.incomplete`` files older than
    ``_INCOMPLETE_STALE_SECONDS`` are removed (an active download keeps its
    file's mtime fresh). For empty ``refs/main``, only the file itself is
    deleted — not the model dir — so already-downloaded small files survive
    and ``snapshot_download`` raises ``LocalEntryNotFoundError`` (which
    fastembed catches and falls through to a network re-download).
    """
    cache = _get_hf_cache()
    if cache is None:
        return

    now = time.time()
    for f in cache.glob("models--*/blobs/*.incomplete"):
        try:
            if now - f.stat().st_mtime > _INCOMPLETE_STALE_SECONDS:
                f.unlink()
                logger.debug(f"Removed stale incomplete download: {f}")
        except OSError:
            pass

    for refs_main in cache.glob("models--*/refs/main"):
        try:
            if refs_main.stat().st_size == 0:
                refs_main.unlink()
                logger.warning(
                    f"Removed empty refs/main for "
                    f"{refs_main.parent.parent.name}"

def test_unload_releases_refcount(self):
        """unload() should decrement the cache refcount."""
        from cogz.embedding import EmbeddingEngine

        EmbeddingEngine._cache.clear()
        engine = EmbeddingEngine(model_name="test-model")

        # Simulate loaded state
        fake_model = object()
        EmbeddingEngine._cache.put("test-model", fake_model)
        engine._model = fake_model
        engine._loaded = True

        stats = EmbeddingEngine._cache.stats()
        assert stats["active_refs"] == 1

        engine.unload()

        stats = EmbeddingEngine._cache.stats()
        assert stats["active_refs"] == 0
        assert stats["evictable"] == 1  # cached but no active users
        assert not engine._loaded

        EmbeddingEngine._cache.clear()

def _refine_search_results(
        self,
        fused: list[SearchResult],
        query: str,
        top_k: int,
        options: SearchOptions,
    ) -> list[SearchResult]:
        """Apply auto-widening and reranking to fused search results.

        If results are insufficient and exploratory scope is enabled,
        widens the search. Then applies cross-encoder reranking if
        available, or sorts by score as a fallback.
        """
        # Auto-widen if results are insufficient
        # scope_mode takes precedence: strict_scope forces auto_widen off.
        effective_auto_widen = options.auto_widen and options.scope_mode == "exploratory_scope"
        if effective_auto_widen and len(fused) < SEARCH_AUTO_WIDEN_THRESHOLD:
            fused = self._auto_widen(
                query, top_k, options, fused,
            )

        # Reranking
        if options.rerank and self.reranker and self.reranker.enabled and fused:
            fused = self.reranker.rerank(query, fused, top_k=top_k)
        else:
            fused.sort(key=lambda r: (r.score, r.entity_id), reverse=True)
            fused = fused[:top_k]
        return fused

def _auto_widen(
        self,
        query: str,
        top_k: int,
        options: SearchOptions,
        current: list[SearchResult],
    ) -> list[SearchResult]:
        """Progressively relax taxonomy filters to find more results.

        Three levels: drop domain → drop subcategory → drop project.
        Stops as soon as enough results are found.
        """
        fused = current
        seen = {(r.entity_type, r.entity_id) for r in fused}

        def _merge(wider: list[SearchResult]) -> None:
            nonlocal fused
            for r in wider:
                if (r.entity_type, r.entity_id) not in seen:
                    fused.append(r)
                    seen.add((r.entity_type, r.entity_id))

        # Level 1: drop domain
        if options.domain is not None and len(fused) < SEARCH_AUTO_WIDEN_THRESHOLD:
            wider = self.search(
                query, top_k, options.project, options.subcategory, None, options.entity_types,
                mode=options.mode, rerank=False, auto_widen=False,
                snippet_chars=options.snippet_chars,
                include_superseded=options.include_superseded,
            )
            for r in wider:
                r.scope_relaxation = "domain"
            _merge(wider)

        # Level 2: drop subcategory
        if options.subcategory is not None and len(fused) < SEARCH_AUTO_WIDEN_THRESHOLD:
            wider = self.search(
                query, top_k, options.project, None, options.domain, options.entity_types,
                mode=options.mode, rerank=False, auto_widen=False,
                snippet_chars=options.snippet_chars,

"""Search engine for CogZ (Phase 1B).

Hybrid search combining FTS5 (keyword) and vector (semantic) search
with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF). Auto-widens the search scope when
initial results are insufficient.

Flow:
  1. FTS5 search on all text-bearing tables (BM25 ranked)
     - Natural language queries are rewritten to FTS5 OR syntax
       to avoid implicit AND matching all terms (which rarely
       matches any document with multi-word questions).
  2. Vector search on vec_entities (cosine distance via sqlite-vec)
  3. RRF fusion of both result sets
  4. Optional reranker cross-encoder reranking
  5. Snippet extraction for display

Auto-widen: if initial results < threshold, relax taxonomy filters
in three levels: drop domain, then subcategory, then project.

class SearchEngine:
    """Hybrid search engine combining FTS5 and vector search.

    Args:
        storage: The Storage instance.
        embedding: Optional EmbeddingEngine for vector search (code entities).
        knowledge_embedding: Optional EmbeddingEngine for non-code entities
            (observations, rules, patterns). Falls back to `embedding` if None.
        reranker: Optional RerankerEngine for cross-encoder reranking.
        splitter: Optional TextSplitter for chunk-level search.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        storage: Storage,
        embedding=None,
        knowledge_embedding=None,
        reranker: RerankerEngine | None = None,
        splitter: TextSplitter | None = None,
    ):
        self.storage = storage
        self.embedding = embedding
        self.knowledge_embedding = knowledge_embedding or embedding
        self.reranker = reranker or RerankerEngine(enabled=False)
        self.splitter = splitter or TextSplitter()

    @staticmethod
    def _rewrite_fts_query(query: str) -> str:
        """Rewrite a natural language query for FTS5.

        FTS5 uses implicit AND for space-separated terms, meaning every
        term must match. With natural language questions (e.g., "How does
        the auth middleware validate JWT tokens?"), this almost never
        matches any document because documents rarely contain all the
        exact words.

        This method converts NL queries to FTS5 OR syntax so that
        documents matching any significant term are returned, ranked
        by BM25 relevance. Stopwords are removed to reduce noise.

def _clean_broken_cache() -> None:
    """Remove orphaned download artifacts that prevent model loading.

    huggingface_hub leaves ``.incomplete`` temp files when a download is
    interrupted and never garbage-collects them. A failed initial download
    can also leave ``refs/main`` empty (0 bytes), which causes
    ``snapshot_download(local_files_only=True)`` to return the ``snapshots/``
    parent dir instead of the hash subdir — onnxruntime then fails with
    NoSuchFile because ``snapshots/model.onnx`` doesn't exist. Both
    conditions block the model from ever loading and compound with each
    retry: every failed attempt adds another dead partial, filling the disk
    and making the next download fail even sooner.

    Safe with concurrent downloads: only ``.incomplete`` files older than
    ``_INCOMPLETE_STALE_SECONDS`` are removed (an active download keeps its
    file's mtime fresh). For empty ``refs/main``, only the file itself is
    deleted — not the model dir — so already-downloaded small files survive
    and ``snapshot_download`` raises ``LocalEntryNotFoundError`` (which
    fastembed catches and falls through to a network re-download).
    """
    cache = _get_hf_cache()
    if cache is None:
        return

    now = time.time()
    for f in cache.glob("models--*/blobs/*.incomplete"):
        try:
            if now - f.stat().st_mtime > _INCOMPLETE_STALE_SECONDS:
                f.unlink()
                logger.debug(f"Removed stale incomplete download: {f}")
        except OSError:
            pass

    for refs_main in cache.glob("models--*/refs/main"):
        try:
            if refs_main.stat().st_size == 0:
                refs_main.unlink()
                logger.warning(
                    f"Removed empty refs/main for "
                    f"{refs_main.parent.parent.name}"

def test_held_out_constrained_runtime(tmp_path: Path):
    """Constrained runtime: exercise lifecycle with FTS-only search.

    Runs the lifecycle with FTS-only search (no embeddings), no reranking,
    and limited graph expansion. Verifies that the system degrades
    functionally without optional model dependencies.
    """
    adapter = _setup_runtime(tmp_path)
    try:
        result = run_lifecycle_scenario("constrained-runtime", adapter, mode="in_process")
        assert result.passed, f"Scenario failed: {result.errors}"
        assert len(result.tool_trace) > 0, "No operations were executed"
        scenario_gates = [g for g in result.gates if g.execution_surface]
        for gate in scenario_gates:
            assert gate.execution_surface == "in_process", f"Gate {gate.name} has wrong surface: {gate.execution_surface}"
        # Context must have content even in constrained mode
        context_gates = [g for g in result.gates if g.name == "context_has_content"]
        assert len(context_gates) >= 1, "No context_has_content gates found"
    finally:
        adapter.state.close()

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CogZ lifecycle hook for Devin CLI
#
# Usage: cogz-hook.sh <EventName>
# Reads JSON event data from stdin, calls `cogz capture-event`, writes response to stdout.
#
# This is a thin wrapper — all logic lives in the Python LifecycleCoordinator.
# The adapter (DevinAdapter) handles event name translation and response format.
#
# Install via: cogz hooks install devin --repo .
# Config written to: .devin/hooks.v1.json
#
# Failures are NOT silent: stderr is forwarded to the terminal, a structured
# error JSON is emitted, and the exit code is non-zero. A rate-limited error
# log is written to $COGZ_HOOK_ERROR_LOG (default:
# ~/.local/share/cogz/hook-errors.log).

set -euo pipefail

EVENT="${1:?Usage: cogz-hook.sh <EventName>}"
AGENT="devin"

# Read event data from stdin (Devin sends JSON payload on stdin)
INPUT=$(cat)

# Call CogZ lifecycle coordinator. --payload @- reads from stdin.
# stderr is NOT suppressed — errors must be visible.
# On failure, output a structured error JSON and record to error log.
ERROR_LOG="${COGZ_HOOK_ERROR_LOG:-$HOME/.local/share/cogz/hook-errors.log}"

def _clean_broken_cache() -> None:
    """Remove orphaned download artifacts that prevent model loading.

    huggingface_hub leaves ``.incomplete`` temp files when a download is
    interrupted and never garbage-collects them. A failed initial download
    can also leave ``refs/main`` empty (0 bytes), which causes
    ``snapshot_download(local_files_only=True)`` to return the ``snapshots/``
    parent dir instead of the hash subdir — onnxruntime then fails with
    NoSuchFile because ``snapshots/model.onnx`` doesn't exist. Both
    conditions block the model from ever loading and compound with each
    retry: every failed attempt adds another dead partial, filling the disk
    and making the next download fail even sooner.

    Safe with concurrent downloads: only ``.incomplete`` files older than
    ``_INCOMPLETE_STALE_SECONDS`` are removed (an active download keeps its
    file's mtime fresh). For empty ``refs/main``, only the file itself is
    deleted — not the model dir — so already-downloaded small files survive
    and ``snapshot_download`` raises ``LocalEntryNotFoundError`` (which
    fastembed catches and falls through to a network re-download).
    """
    cache = _get_hf_cache()
    if cache is None:
        return

    now = time.time()
    for f in cache.glob("models--*/blobs/*.incomplete"):
        try:
            if now - f.stat().st_mtime > _INCOMPLETE_STALE_SECONDS:
                f.unlink()
                logger.debug(f"Removed stale incomplete download: {f}")
        except OSError:
            pass

    for refs_main in cache.glob("models--*/refs/main"):
        try:
            if refs_main.stat().st_size == 0:
                refs_main.unlink()
                logger.warning(
                    f"Removed empty refs/main for "
                    f"{refs_main.parent.parent.name}"

def _load_adjacency(
        self,
        edge_types: list[str] | None = None,
        project_id: str | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
        """Load graph from SQLite into an in-memory adjacency list.

        Args:
            edge_types: Filter to specific edge types. None = all edges.
            project_id: Filter to specific project. None = all projects.

        Returns:
            Directed adjacency list: {source_id: [target_id, ...]}.
            Isolated nodes (no edges) appear as keys with empty lists.
        """
        # Load all nodes to ensure isolated nodes are included
        nodes = self.storage.query_nodes(project_id=project_id)
        adj: dict[str, list[str]] = {n["id"]: [] for n in nodes}

        # Load edges
        with self.storage._connect() as conn:
            sql = "SELECT source_id, target_id, type FROM edges WHERE 1=1"
            params: list[Any] = []
            if edge_types:
                placeholders = ",".join("?" * len(edge_types))
                sql += f" AND type IN ({placeholders})"
                params.extend(edge_types)
            if project_id:
                sql += " AND (source_id IN (SELECT id FROM nodes WHERE project_id = ?) OR target_id IN (SELECT id FROM nodes WHERE project_id = ?))"
                params.extend([project_id, project_id])
            rows = conn.execute(sql, params).fetchall()

        for row in rows:
            src = row["source_id"]
            tgt = row["target_id"]
            adj.setdefault(src, []).append(tgt)
            adj.setdefault(tgt, [])  # ensure target is in adjacency

        return adj

class Storage:
    """Primary SQLite storage for CogZ.

    Threading Contract
    ------------------
    Storage uses a **single persistent SQLite connection** (``self._conn``)
    with shared ``_in_transaction`` state.  This design is intentional:

    - SQLite WAL mode allows concurrent readers, but a single writer.
    - The persistent connection avoids per-request connection overhead.
    - Transaction nesting is tracked via ``_in_transaction`` to prevent
      nested BEGINs.

    **Consequence:** Storage instances are **NOT thread-safe**.  Concurrent
    access from multiple threads or interleaved async tasks will race on
    ``_in_transaction`` and connection state.

    **Mitigation:** The REST API uses ``SerializationMiddleware`` (see
    ``api.py``) to acquire an ``asyncio.Lock`` around every request,
    serializing all Storage access.  CLI and MCP server are single-threaded
    by design.  Any new entry point that touches Storage from multiple
    threads MUST acquire a lock before accessing the shared instance.

    The ``_connect()`` context manager yields the shared connection.
    Callers must not hold references to the connection outside the
    ``with`` block, as the connection may be closed and reopened between
    calls (health check in ``_get_conn``).
    """

    def __init__(self, db_path: Path | str, *, embedding_dim: int | None = None,
                 config_store: Any = None):
        """Initialize the Storage instance and ensure the database exists.

        Args:
            db_path: Path to the SQLite database file.
            embedding_dim: Optional override for the vec0 table dimension.
                If None, uses the EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS constant (default 384).
            config_store: Optional ConfigStore for config-aware checks

"""Tests for embedding cache healing: orphaned .incomplete cleanup and empty
refs/main detection.

huggingface_hub leaves .incomplete temp files when a download is interrupted
and never garbage-collects them. A failed initial download can also leave
refs/main empty, which causes snapshot_download(local_files_only=True) to
return the snapshots/ parent dir instead of the hash subdir, producing a
NoSuchFile error from onnxruntime. _clean_broken_cache() runs before the
model is loaded and removes both conditions so the next load triggers a
clean re-download.

The cleanup is safe with concurrent downloads: only .incomplete files older
than _INCOMPLETE_STALE_SECONDS are removed, and empty refs/main is deleted
as a file (not a dir nuke) so already-downloaded files survive.

sections.title: _clean_broken_cache
sections.content:
def _clean_broken_cache() -> None:
    """Remove orphaned download artifacts that prevent model loading.

    huggingface_hub leaves ``.incomplete`` temp files when a download is
    interrupted and never garbage-collects them. A failed initial download
    can also leave ``refs/main`` empty (0 bytes), which causes
    ``snapshot_download(local_files_only=True)`` to return the ``snapshots/``
    parent dir instead of the hash subdir — onnxruntime then fails with
    NoSuchFile because ``snapshots/model.onnx`` doesn't exist. Both
    conditions block the model from ever loading and compound with each
    retry: every failed attempt adds another dead partial, filling the disk
    and making the next download fail even sooner.

    Safe with concurrent downloads: only ``.incomplete`` files older than
    ``_INCOMPLETE_STALE_SECONDS`` are removed (an active download keeps its
    file's mtime fresh). For empty ``refs/main``, only the file itself is
    deleted — not the model dir — so already-downloaded small files survive
    and ``snapshot_download`` raises ``LocalEntryNotFoundError`` (which
    fastembed catches and falls through to a network re-download).
    """
    cache = _get_hf_cache()
    if cache is None:
        return

    now = time.time()
    for f in cache.glob("models--*/blobs/*.incomplete"):
        try:
            if now - f.stat().st_mtime > _INCOMPLETE_STALE_SECONDS:
                f.unlink()
                logger.debug(f"Removed stale incomplete download: {f}")
        except OSError:
            pass

    for refs_main in cache.glob("models--*/refs/main"):
        try:
            if refs_main.stat().st_size == 0:
                refs_main.unlink()
                logger.warning(
                    f"Removed empty refs/main for "
                    f"{refs_main.parent.parent.name}"

def _load_model(self) -> None:
        """Load the embedding model (lazy, on first use)."""
        if self._loaded:
            return

        # Evict idle cached models past their TTL before attempting load.
        # This frees memory from models that were unloaded but still cached.
        self._cache.evict_idle(self.idle_ttl)

        # Check the shared model cache first — if another EmbeddingEngine
        # with the same model_name already loaded the model, reuse it.
        # This prevents loading the same ONNX model multiple times
        # (each load ~67-250MB depending on model).
        cached = self._cache.get(self.model_name)
        if cached is not None:
            self._model = cached
            self._loaded = True
            self._last_used = time.time()

        # Not in cache — need to load. First, try to free memory by
        # evicting unused cached models (refcount=0) if memory is low.

def _get_hf_cache() -> Path | None:
    """Resolve the HuggingFace hub cache directory.

    fastembed uses huggingface_hub's default cache (HF_HOME/hub or
    ~/.cache/huggingface/hub). We resolve it lazily so the import
    doesn't fail if huggingface_hub isn't installed yet.
    """
    try:
        from huggingface_hub.constants import HF_HUB_CACHE
        cache = Path(HF_HUB_CACHE)
        return cache if cache.is_dir() else None
    except Exception:
        return None

sections.content:
def _make_model_dir(cache, repo_slug, *, refs_content=None, incomplete=True,
                    incomplete_age=7200):
    """Create a fake HF cache layout for one model.

    repo_slug: e.g. "BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5"
    refs_content: bytes to write into refs/main. None = don't create the file.
    incomplete_age: age in seconds for .incomplete files (default 2h = stale).
    """
    model_dir_name = f"models--{repo_slug.replace('/', '--')}"
    model_dir = cache / model_dir_name
    blobs = model_dir / "blobs"
    snapshots = model_dir / "snapshots"
    refs = model_dir / "refs"
    blobs.mkdir(parents=True)
    snapshots.mkdir(parents=True)
    refs.mkdir(parents=True)

    # A complete blob + symlink in the snapshot
    (blobs / "aaa").write_bytes(b"model")
    hash_dir = snapshots / "abc123"
    hash_dir.mkdir()
    (hash_dir / "model.onnx").symlink_to("../../blobs/aaa")

    if refs_content is not None:
        (refs / "main").write_bytes(refs_content)

    if incomplete:
        for name in ("bbb.incomplete", "ccc.incomplete"):
            p = blobs / name
            p.write_bytes(b"\x00" * 100)
            old = time.time() - incomplete_age
            os.utime(p, (old, old))

    return model_dir

def _load_model(self) -> None:
        """Load the reranker model (lazy, on first use)."""
        if self._loaded:
            return

        if not self.enabled:
            return

        # Evict idle cached models past their TTL
        self._cache.evict_idle(self.idle_ttl)

        # Check the shared model cache first
        cached = self._cache.get(self.model_name)
        if cached is not None:
            self._model = cached
            self._loaded = True
            self._last_used = time.time()
            return

        # Not in cache — try to free memory by evicting unused entries
        self._cache.evict_for_memory(self.min_free_mb)

        try:
            guard_memory(self.min_free_mb)
        except MemoryError:
            logger.warning("Insufficient RAM for reranker model, disabling reranking")
            self.enabled = False
            return

        try:
            from fastembed.rerank.cross_encoder import TextCrossEncoder
        except ImportError:
            logger.warning("fastembed reranker not installed, reranking disabled")
            self.enabled = False
            return

        try:
            self._model = TextCrossEncoder(model_name=self.model_name)
            self._loaded = True
            self._last_used = time.time()

sections.content:
def _try_embed(self, entity_id: str, text: str,
                   project: str, subcategory: str, domain: str) -> None:
        """Embed text and store vector, if embedding engine is available.

        Embedding failure is non-fatal — the knowledge entry is still stored
        without a vector. The failure is logged and recorded in the event
        log so it can be diagnosed and the entry re-embedded later via
        'cogz maintenance reindex-embeddings'.
        """
        if self._embedding is None:
            return
        try:
            vector, text_hash = self._embedding.embed(text)
            self.storage.store_embedding(
                entity_type="knowledge", entity_id=entity_id,
                embedding=vector, text_hash=text_hash,
                model_name=self._embedding.model_name,
                dimensions=self._embedding.dimensions,
                project=project, subcategory=subcategory, domain=domain,
            )
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning(
                f"Embedding failed for knowledge:{entity_id}: {e}. "
                "Entry stored without vector — run 'cogz maintenance reindex-embeddings' to populate."
            )
            self.storage.record_event("EmbeddingFailed", {
                "entity_type": "knowledge",
                "entity_id": entity_id,
                "error": str(e),
                "project": project,
                "subcategory": subcategory,
            })

def _try_create_weave_edge(
        self,
        e1: dict, e2: dict, sim: float, dry_run: bool,
    ) -> int:
        """Try to create a cross-category weave edge between two entities.

        Protection check: skip if either endpoint is protected (locked,
        high-importance, or VALIDATED/REJECTED rule). Consistent with
        Phase B protection semantics. Returns 1 if edge created/counted, 0 if skipped.
        """
        if self._is_protected(e1["entity_type"], e1["entity_id"]):
            return 0
        if self._is_protected(e2["entity_type"], e2["entity_id"]):
            return 0
        if dry_run:
            return 1
        try:
            with self.storage.transaction():
                self.storage.create_edge(
                    e1["entity_id"], e2["entity_id"], "relates_to",
                    {"cosine_similarity": sim, "cross_category": True},
                )
                # Record mutation in event log for auditability.
                self.storage.record_event("CrossCategoryEdgeCreated", {
                    "source_id": e1["entity_id"],
                    "target_id": e2["entity_id"],
                    "source_type": e1["entity_type"],
                    "target_type": e2["entity_type"],
                    "source_subcategory": e1["subcategory"],
                    "target_subcategory": e2["subcategory"],
                    "cosine_similarity": sim,
                    "phase": "F",
                })
            return 1
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.debug(f"Failed to create cross-category edge: {exc}")
            return 0

def _clean_broken_cache() -> None:
    """Remove orphaned download artifacts that prevent model loading.

    huggingface_hub leaves ``.incomplete`` temp files when a download is
    interrupted and never garbage-collects them. A failed initial download
    can also leave ``refs/main`` empty (0 bytes), which causes
    ``snapshot_download(local_files_only=True)`` to return the ``snapshots/``
    parent dir instead of the hash subdir — onnxruntime then fails with
    NoSuchFile because ``snapshots/model.onnx`` doesn't exist. Both
    conditions block the model from ever loading and compound with each
    retry: every failed attempt adds another dead partial, filling the disk
    and making the next download fail even sooner.

    Safe with concurrent downloads: only ``.incomplete`` files older than
    ``_INCOMPLETE_STALE_SECONDS`` are removed (an active download keeps its
    file's mtime fresh). For empty ``refs/main``, only the file itself is
    deleted — not the model dir — so already-downloaded small files survive
    and ``snapshot_download`` raises ``LocalEntryNotFoundError`` (which
    fastembed catches and falls through to a network re-download).
    """
    cache = _get_hf_cache()
    if cache is None:
        return

    for f in cache.glob("models--*/blobs/*.incomplete"):

def search_vectors(

        subcategory: str | None = None,
        domain: str | None = None,
        entity_types: list[str] | None = None,
        include_superseded: bool = False,
        model_name: str | None = None,
        node_types: list[str] | None = None,
    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """KNN search on vec_entities, scoped by taxonomy.

        Args:
            query_embedding: The query vector.
            k: Number of nearest neighbors to return.
            project: Optional project filter.
            subcategory: Optional subcategory filter.
            domain: Optional domain filter.
            entity_types: Optional list of entity types to include.
            include_superseded: If True, include superseded entities.
            model_name: Optional filter to only return vectors from this model.
            node_types: Optional filter for node types (applies post-query by
                joining to the nodes table to check the `type` column).

        Returns:
            List of dicts with entity_type, entity_id, distance, text_hash,
            model_name, dimensions, project, subcategory, domain.

def query_telemetry(
        self,
        event_type: str | None = None,
        project_id: str | None = None,
        limit: int = 100,
    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Query telemetry events (newest first).

        Args:
            event_type: Optional event type filter.
            project_id: Optional project filter.
            limit: Maximum results (default 100).

        Returns:
            List of telemetry dicts with deserialized payloads.
        """
        with self._connect() as conn:
            sql = "SELECT * FROM telemetry WHERE 1=1"
            params: list[Any] = []
            if event_type:
                sql += " AND event_type = ?"
                params.append(event_type)
            if project_id:
                sql += " AND project_id = ?"
                params.append(project_id)
            sql += " ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?"
            params.append(limit)
            rows = conn.execute(sql, params).fetchall()
            result = []
            for r in rows:
                d = dict(r)
                try:
                    d["payload"] = json.loads(d["payload"])
                except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
                    pass
                result.append(d)
            return result

sections.content:
class Storage:
    """Primary SQLite storage for CogZ.

    Threading Contract
    ------------------
    Storage uses a **single persistent SQLite connection** (``self._conn``)
    with shared ``_in_transaction`` state.  This design is intentional:

    - SQLite WAL mode allows concurrent readers, but a single writer.
    - The persistent connection avoids per-request connection overhead.
    - Transaction nesting is tracked via ``_in_transaction`` to prevent
      nested BEGINs.

    **Consequence:** Storage instances are **NOT thread-safe**.  Concurrent
    access from multiple threads or interleaved async tasks will race on
    ``_in_transaction`` and connection state.

    **Mitigation:** The REST API uses ``SerializationMiddleware`` (see
    ``api.py``) to acquire an ``asyncio.Lock`` around every request,
    serializing all Storage access.  CLI and MCP server are single-threaded
    by design.  Any new entry point that touches Storage from multiple
    threads MUST acquire a lock before accessing the shared instance.

    The ``_connect()`` context manager yields the shared connection.
    Callers must not hold references to the connection outside the
    ``with`` block, as the connection may be closed and reopened between
    calls (health check in ``_get_conn``).
    """

    def __init__(self, db_path: Path | str, *, embedding_dim: int | None = None,
                 config_store: Any = None):
        """Initialize the Storage instance and ensure the database exists.

        Args:
            db_path: Path to the SQLite database file.
            embedding_dim: Optional override for the vec0 table dimension.
                If None, uses the EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS constant (default 384).
            config_store: Optional ConfigStore for config-aware checks
                (e.g., telemetry enablement). When None, only env vars
                control feature flags.

def get_edges(self, source_id: str | None = None, target_id: str | None = None, edge_type: str | None = None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Retrieve edges with optional source, target, and type filters.

        Args:
            source_id: Filter by source node ID. Defaults to None.
            target_id: Filter by target node ID. Defaults to None.
            edge_type: Filter by exact edge type. Defaults to None.

        Returns:
            list[dict[str, Any]]: List of matching edge dictionaries with deserialized properties.
        """
        with self._connect() as conn:
            sql = "SELECT * FROM edges WHERE 1=1"
            params: list[Any] = []
            if source_id:
                sql += " AND source_id = ?"
                params.append(source_id)
            if target_id:
                sql += " AND target_id = ?"
                params.append(target_id)
            if edge_type:
                sql += " AND type = ?"
                params.append(edge_type)
            rows = conn.execute(sql, params).fetchall()
            return [dict(r) | {"properties": json.loads(r["properties"])} for r in rows]

sections.title: _fetch_entities_for_reindex
sections.content:
def _fetch_entities_for_reindex(
        self,
        storage: Any,
        etype: str,
        spec: EntitySpec,
        project: str | None,
    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Fetch entities from storage for reindexing.

        For "node" entity type with code model, filters to only code node
        types (Function, Class, File, etc.). Knowledge entries stored as
        nodes are excluded — they have their own table entries with bge-base
        embeddings. Also fetches consolidation_status for vec_entities sync.
        """
        from .constants import CODE_ENTITY_TYPES, CODE_NODE_TYPES

        is_code = etype in CODE_ENTITY_TYPES
        table = spec.table
        text_expr = spec.text_expr
        proj_col = spec.project_col

        with storage._connect() as conn:
            status_expr = "consolidation_status" if "consolidation_status" in [
                row["name"] for row in conn.execute(f"PRAGMA table_info({table})").fetchall()
            ] else "'active' as consolidation_status"
            if etype == "node" and is_code:
                placeholders = ", ".join(["?"] * len(CODE_NODE_TYPES))
                sql = f"SELECT id, {text_expr} as text, {proj_col} as project, subcategory, domain, {status_expr} FROM {table} WHERE type IN ({placeholders})"
                params: list[Any] = list(CODE_NODE_TYPES)
                if project:
                    sql += f" AND {proj_col} = ?"
                    params.append(project)
            else:
                sql = f"SELECT id, {text_expr} as text, {proj_col} as project, subcategory, domain, {status_expr} FROM {table}"
                params = []
                if project:
                    sql += f" WHERE {proj_col} = ?"
                    params.append(project)
            rows = conn.execute(sql, params).fetchall()
            return [dict(r) for r in rows if r["text"]]

sections.title: _check_import_targets_test_dir
sections.content:
def _check_import_targets_test_dir(
        self,
        imp: str,
        file_nodes: list[dict[str, Any]],
        file_path: str,
        repo_path: Path,
        seen_src_test: set[tuple[str, str]],
    ) -> bool:
        """Check if an import targets a test directory; record constraint if so.

        Returns True if a match was found (caller should break the import loop).
        """
        file_rel = Path(file_path).relative_to(repo_path)
        file_dir = Path(file_path).parent.name
        for other in file_nodes:
            other_rel = Path(other["path"]).relative_to(repo_path)
            other_dir = other_rel.parent.name
            if other_dir == file_dir:
                continue
            if "test" in other_dir.lower() and (imp == other_dir or imp.startswith(other_dir + ".")):
                pair = (file_dir, other_dir)
                if pair not in seen_src_test:
                    seen_src_test.add(pair)
                    self.knowledge.create(
                        "constraint",
                        f"Source code depends on tests: {file_dir} -> {other_dir}",
                        f"File `{file_rel}` imports from test directory `{other_dir}/`. "
                        "Source code should never depend on test utilities.",
                        fmt="markdown",
                        auto_generated=True,
                    )
                return True
        return False

sections.title: query_entities_by_status
sections.content:
def query_entities_by_status(
        self, status: str, entity_type: str | None = None,
        project: str | None = None, subcategory: str | None = None,
    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Query entities by consolidation status, optionally filtered by taxonomy."""
        types = [entity_type] if entity_type else [
            etype for etype in self._ENTITY_TABLES if etype not in ("node", "metric")
        ]
        results: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        for etype in types:
            if etype in ("node", "metric"):
                # Graph nodes and metrics have no consolidation_status column.
                continue
            table = self._ENTITY_TABLES[etype]
            proj_col = "project_id" if etype == "node" else "project"
            conditions = ["consolidation_status = ?"]
            params: list[Any] = [status]
            if project is not None:
                conditions.append(f"{proj_col} = ?")
                params.append(project)
            if subcategory is not None:
                conditions.append("subcategory = ?")
                params.append(subcategory)
            where = " WHERE " + " AND ".join(conditions)
            with self._connect() as conn:
                rows = conn.execute(
                    f"SELECT id, {proj_col} as project, subcategory, domain, consolidation_status FROM {table}{where}",
                    params,
                ).fetchall()
                for row in rows:
                    results.append({
                        "entity_type": etype,
                        "entity_id": row["id"],
                        "project": row["project"],
                        "subcategory": row["subcategory"],
                        "domain": row["domain"],
                        "status": row["consolidation_status"],
                    })
        return results

class Storage:
    """Primary SQLite storage for CogZ.

    Threading Contract
    ------------------
    Storage uses a **single persistent SQLite connection** (``self._conn``)
    with shared ``_in_transaction`` state.  This design is intentional:

    - SQLite WAL mode allows concurrent readers, but a single writer.
    - The persistent connection avoids per-request connection overhead.
    - Transaction nesting is tracked via ``_in_transaction`` to prevent
      nested BEGINs.

    **Consequence:** Storage instances are **NOT thread-safe**.  Concurrent
    access from multiple threads or interleaved async tasks will race on
    ``_in_transaction`` and connection state.

    **Mitigation:** The REST API uses ``SerializationMiddleware`` (see
    ``api.py``) to acquire an ``asyncio.Lock`` around every request,
    serializing all Storage access.  CLI and MCP server are single-threaded
    by design.  Any new entry point that touches Storage from multiple
    threads MUST acquire a lock before accessing the shared instance.

    The ``_connect()`` context manager yields the shared connection.
    Callers must not hold references to the connection outside the
    ``with`` block, as the connection may be closed and reopened between
    calls (health check in ``_get_conn``).
    """

    def __init__(self, db_path: Path | str, *, embedding_dim: int | None = None,
                 config_store: Any = None):
        """Initialize the Storage instance and ensure the database exists.

        Args:
            db_path: Path to the SQLite database file.
            embedding_dim: Optional override for the vec0 table dimension.
                If None, uses the EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS constant (default 384).
            config_store: Optional ConfigStore for config-aware checks
                (e.g., telemetry enablement). When None, only env vars
                control feature flags.

def _build_fts_search_sql(
        self,
        fts_table: str,
        base_table: str,
        text_cols: list[str],
        project_col: str | None,
        q: _FtsSearchQuery,
    ) -> tuple[str, list[Any]]:
        """Build the FTS5 search SQL and params.

        Constructs the WHERE conditions (taxonomy filters, node type
        filter, status filter), snippet expression, and SELECT clause
        for the FTS5 search query.
        """
        # Prefix columns with fts_table to avoid ambiguity when a JOIN
        # to the base table is added for consolidation status filtering.
        conditions = []
        params: list[Any] = []
        if q.project and project_col is not None:
            conditions.append(f"{fts_table}.{project_col} = ?")
            params.append(q.project)
        if q.subcategory:
            conditions.append(f"{fts_table}.subcategory = ?")
            params.append(q.subcategory)
        if q.domain:
            conditions.append(f"{fts_table}.domain = ?")
            params.append(q.domain)
        # Node type filter (only for fts_nodes which has a `type` column)

            placeholders = ", ".join(["?"] * len(q.node_types))

        """If the file move fails during archive, DB should be rolled back."""
        kid = kl.create("architecture", "Archive Fail", "Content",
                       repo_path=tmp_repo_with_cogz)
        entry_before = kl.get(kid)
        assert entry_before["consolidation_status"] == "active"

        # Make the archive directory read-only to cause move failure
        archive_dir = tmp_repo_with_cogz / ".cogz" / "knowledge" / "archive" / "architecture"
        archive_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        archive_dir.chmod(0o444)

        try:

                kl.archive_knowledge(kid)

            assert entry_after["consolidation_status"] == "active"

        fmt = entry.get("format", "markdown")

def build_file_context(
        self,
        file_path: str | Path,
        project: str | None = None,
        subcategory: str | None = None,
        domain: str | None = None,
    ) -> ContextPack:
        """Build a context pack for a specific file.

        Args:
            file_path: The path of the file to build context for.
            project: Optional taxonomy project filter.
            subcategory: Optional taxonomy subcategory filter.
            domain: Optional taxonomy domain filter.

        Returns:
            A context pack containing file metadata, functions, and classes.
        """
        sources: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        content: dict[str, Any] = {}

        file_name = str(file_path)
        # Query all File nodes and find exact match on relative path
        all_files = self.graph.query_nodes(node_type="File", project_id=project, subcategory=subcategory, domain=domain)
        file_nodes = [f for f in all_files if f["label"] == file_name]
        if not file_nodes:
            # Fallback: match by basename if full path not found
            basename = Path(file_path).name
            file_nodes = [f for f in all_files if f["label"].endswith(basename)]
        if file_nodes:
            file_node = file_nodes[0]
            file_id = file_node["id"]
            content["file"] = {"label": file_node["label"], "id": file_id}

  - project: top-level project/context identifier (default: "dev")

sections.content:
def _collect_file_learning_context(
        self,
        file_name: str,
        learning_kwargs: dict[str, Any],
        content: dict[str, Any],
        sources: list[dict[str, Any]],
    ) -> None:
        """Collect learning entities (observations, patterns, rules) mentioning a file."""
        if self.learning is None:
            return
        obs = sorted(self.learning.query_observations(**learning_kwargs), key=lambda e: e.get("created_at", ""), reverse=True)
        file_obs = [o for o in obs if file_name.lower() in o.get("statement", "").lower()]
        if file_obs:
            content["related_observations"] = [o["statement"] for o in file_obs[:5]]
            sources.append({"type": "learning", "query": "observations mentioning file", "count": len(file_obs)})

        # Patterns and rules relevant to this file
        patterns = sorted(self.learning.query_patterns(**learning_kwargs), key=lambda e: e.get("created_at", ""), reverse=True)
        file_patterns = [p["statement"] for p in patterns if file_name.lower() in p.get("statement", "").lower() or any(file_name.lower() in obs_id.lower() for obs_id in p.get("supporting_observation_ids", []))][:5]
        if file_patterns:
            content["relevant_patterns"] = file_patterns
            sources.append({"type": "learning", "query": "patterns mentioning file", "count": len(file_patterns)})

        rules = sorted(self.learning.query_rules(**learning_kwargs), key=lambda e: e.get("created_at", ""), reverse=True)
        validated = [r for r in rules if r.get("properties", {}).get("status") == "VALIDATED"]
        file_rules = [r["statement"] for r in validated if file_name.lower() in r.get("statement", "").lower()][:5]
        if file_rules:
            content["relevant_rules"] = file_rules
            sources.append({"type": "learning", "query": "rules mentioning file", "count": len(file_rules)})

sections.title: _try_embed
sections.content:
def _try_embed(self, entity_id: str, text: str,
                   project: str, subcategory: str, domain: str) -> None:
        """Embed text and store vector, if embedding engine is available.

        Embedding failure is non-fatal — the knowledge entry is still stored
        without a vector. The failure is logged and recorded in the event
        log so it can be diagnosed and the entry re-embedded later via
        'cogz maintenance reindex-embeddings'.
        """
        if self._embedding is None:
            return
        try:
            vector, text_hash = self._embedding.embed(text)
            self.storage.store_embedding(
                entity_type="knowledge", entity_id=entity_id,
                embedding=vector, text_hash=text_hash,
                model_name=self._embedding.model_name,
                dimensions=self._embedding.dimensions,
                project=project, subcategory=subcategory, domain=domain,
            )
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning(
                f"Embedding failed for knowledge:{entity_id}: {e}. "
                "Entry stored without vector — run 'cogz maintenance reindex-embeddings' to populate."
            )
            self.storage.record_event("EmbeddingFailed", {
                "entity_type": "knowledge",
                "entity_id": entity_id,
                "error": str(e),
                "project": project,
                "subcategory": subcategory,
            })

def _refine_search_results(
        self,
        fused: list[SearchResult],
        query: str,
        top_k: int,
        options: SearchOptions,
    ) -> list[SearchResult]:
        """Apply auto-widening and reranking to fused search results.

        If results are insufficient and exploratory scope is enabled,
        widens the search. Then applies cross-encoder reranking if
        available, or sorts by score as a fallback.
        """
        # Auto-widen if results are insufficient
        # scope_mode takes precedence: strict_scope forces auto_widen off.
        effective_auto_widen = options.auto_widen and options.scope_mode == "exploratory_scope"
        if effective_auto_widen and len(fused) < SEARCH_AUTO_WIDEN_THRESHOLD:
            fused = self._auto_widen(
                query, top_k, options, fused,
            )

        # Reranking
        if options.rerank and self.reranker and self.reranker.enabled and fused:
            fused = self.reranker.rerank(query, fused, top_k=top_k)
        else:
            fused.sort(key=lambda r: (r.score, r.entity_id), reverse=True)
            fused = fused[:top_k]
        return fused

def _auto_widen(
        self,
        query: str,
        top_k: int,
        options: SearchOptions,
        current: list[SearchResult],
    ) -> list[SearchResult]:
        """Progressively relax taxonomy filters to find more results.

        Three levels: drop domain → drop subcategory → drop project.
        Stops as soon as enough results are found.
        """
        fused = current
        seen = {(r.entity_type, r.entity_id) for r in fused}

        def _merge(wider: list[SearchResult]) -> None:
            nonlocal fused
            for r in wider:
                if (r.entity_type, r.entity_id) not in seen:
                    fused.append(r)
                    seen.add((r.entity_type, r.entity_id))

        # Level 1: drop domain
        if options.domain is not None and len(fused) < SEARCH_AUTO_WIDEN_THRESHOLD:
            wider = self.search(
                query, top_k, options.project, options.subcategory, None, options.entity_types,
                mode=options.mode, rerank=False, auto_widen=False,
                snippet_chars=options.snippet_chars,
                include_superseded=options.include_superseded,
            )
            for r in wider:
                r.scope_relaxation = "domain"
            _merge(wider)

        # Level 2: drop subcategory
        if options.subcategory is not None and len(fused) < SEARCH_AUTO_WIDEN_THRESHOLD:
            wider = self.search(
                query, top_k, options.project, None, options.domain, options.entity_types,

            sql = "SELECT * FROM telemetry WHERE 1=1"
            params: list[Any] = []
            if event_type:
                sql += " AND event_type = ?"
                params.append(event_type)
            if project_id:
                sql += " AND project_id = ?"
                params.append(project_id)
            sql += " ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?"
            params.append(limit)
            rows = conn.execute(sql, params).fetchall()
            result = []
            for r in rows:
                d = dict(r)
                try:
                    d["payload"] = json.loads(d["payload"])
                except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
                    pass
                result.append(d)
            return result

def _collect_file_learning_context(
        self,
        file_name: str,
        learning_kwargs: dict[str, Any],
        content: dict[str, Any],
        sources: list[dict[str, Any]],
    ) -> None:
        """Collect learning entities (observations, patterns, rules) mentioning a file."""
        if self.learning is None:
            return
        obs = sorted(self.learning.query_observations(**learning_kwargs), key=lambda e: e.get("created_at", ""), reverse=True)
        file_obs = [o for o in obs if file_name.lower() in o.get("statement", "").lower()]
        if file_obs:
            content["related_observations"] = [o["statement"] for o in file_obs[:5]]
            sources.append({"type": "learning", "query": "observations mentioning file", "count": len(file_obs)})

        # Patterns and rules relevant to this file
        patterns = sorted(self.learning.query_patterns(**learning_kwargs), key=lambda e: e.get("created_at", ""), reverse=True)
        file_patterns = [p["statement"] for p in patterns if file_name.lower() in p.get("statement", "").lower() or any(file_name.lower() in obs_id.lower() for obs_id in p.get("supporting_observation_ids", []))][:5]
        if file_patterns:
            content["relevant_patterns"] = file_patterns
            sources.append({"type": "learning", "query": "patterns mentioning file", "count": len(file_patterns)})

        rules = sorted(self.learning.query_rules(**learning_kwargs), key=lambda e: e.get("created_at", ""), reverse=True)
        validated = [r for r in rules if r.get("properties", {}).get("status") == "VALIDATED"]
        file_rules = [r["statement"] for r in validated if file_name.lower() in r.get("statement", "").lower()][:5]
        if file_rules:
            content["relevant_rules"] = file_rules
            sources.append({"type": "learning", "query": "rules mentioning file", "count": len(file_rules)})

        Phase 3.5: Non-destructive incremental sync.
        - Parse short ID from filename, full UUID from header
        - If UUID exists and content_hash matches: skip

        - If UUID is new: insert
        - If DB record exists but file is missing: mark orphaned
        - Preserves consolidation_status, importance, consolidation_locked

"""Replay agent hook events through the public capture operation."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Iterable
from typing import Any

from .base import BenchmarkAdapter


class HookReplayAdapter:
    """Small adapter for deterministic hook event replay scenarios."""

    def __init__(self, delegate: BenchmarkAdapter):
        self.delegate = delegate

    def replay(self, events: Iterable[dict[str, Any]], **scope: Any) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        results = []
        for item in events:
            results.append(
                self.delegate.capture_event(
                    item.get("agent", "fixture-agent"),
                    item["event"],
                    item.get("payload", {}),
                    **scope,
                )
            )
        return results

    spec = SCENARIOS["code-context"]
    adapter = apply_baseline(adapter, baseline)
    result = _base_result(spec, mode, baseline, seed)
    env = _gate_env(result)
    trace = ToolTrace()
    try:
        responses: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
        for operation, kwargs in (
            ("index_repository", {"mode": "incremental"}),
            ("search", {"query": "cache", "top_k": 10}),
            ("get_context", {"query": "cache", "limit": 10}),
            ("build_context_pack", {"pack_type": "repository", "target": "fixture-repo"}),
        ):
            event = trace.record(operation, kwargs)
            response = getattr(adapter, operation)(**kwargs)
            event.finish(result=response)
            responses[operation] = response

        search_resp = responses.get("search", {})
        search_result_texts = _extract_result_texts(search_resp)
        index_resp = responses.get("index_repository", {})
        context_resp = responses.get("get_context", {})
        pack_resp = responses.get("build_context_pack", {})

        stats = index_resp.get("stats", {}) if isinstance(index_resp, dict) else {}
        search_result_ids = _extract_result_ids(search_resp)

sections.title: _detect_ram_mb_windows
sections.content:
def _detect_ram_mb_windows(self) -> int:
        """Detect total system RAM in MB on Windows via GlobalMemoryStatusEx."""
        try:
            import ctypes
            class MEMORYSTATUSEX(ctypes.Structure):
                _fields_ = [
                    ("dwLength", ctypes.c_ulong),
                    ("dwMemoryLoad", ctypes.c_ulong),
                    ("ullTotalPhys", ctypes.c_ulonglong),
                    ("ullAvailPhys", ctypes.c_ulonglong),
                    ("ullTotalPageFile", ctypes.c_ulonglong),
                    ("ullAvailPageFile", ctypes.c_ulonglong),
                    ("ullTotalVirtual", ctypes.c_ulonglong),
                    ("ullAvailVirtual", ctypes.c_ulonglong),
                    ("ullAvailExtendedVirtual", ctypes.c_ulonglong),
                ]
            stat = MEMORYSTATUSEX()
            stat.dwLength = ctypes.sizeof(stat)
            ctypes.windll.kernel32.GlobalMemoryStatusEx(ctypes.byref(stat))
            return stat.ullTotalPhys // (1024 * 1024)
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.debug(f"RAM detection via Windows API failed: {exc}")
            return 0

def get_recent_events_by_category(
        self,
        category: str,
        event_type: str = "ObservationRecorded",
        limit: int = 20,
    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Get recent events filtered by a JSON payload category field.

        Args:
            category: The category value to filter on (checks payload->'$.category').
            event_type: The event type to filter on. Defaults to "ObservationRecorded".
            limit: Maximum number of events to return.

        Returns:
            List of event dicts with type, payload (dict), and created_at.
        """
        try:
            with self._connect() as conn:
                rows = conn.execute(
                    "SELECT type, payload, created_at FROM events "
                    "WHERE type = ? "
                    "AND json_extract(payload, '$.category') = ? "
                    "ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?",
                    (event_type, category, limit),
                ).fetchall()
                return [self._parse_event_payload(r) for r in rows]
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.warning(f"Failed to query recent events by category: {exc}")
            return []

def extract(self, repo_path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Extract PHP ecosystem metadata from the repository.

        Args:
            repo_path: Path to the repository root directory.

        Returns:
            A dict with keys: language, package_managers, frameworks,
            dependencies, and manifests.
        """
        data: dict[str, Any] = {
            "language": self.language,
            "package_managers": ["composer"],
            "frameworks": set(),
            "dependencies": [],
            "manifests": [],
        }
        for manifest_path in bounded_rglob(repo_path, "composer.json"):
            data["manifests"].append(str(manifest_path.relative_to(repo_path)))
            parsed = self._parse_composer_json(manifest_path)
            if parsed:
                data["dependencies"].extend(parsed.get("dependencies", []))
                if parsed.get("frameworks"):
                    data["frameworks"].update(parsed["frameworks"])
        data["frameworks"] = list(data["frameworks"])
        return data

sections.content:
def query_events(
        self,
        event_type: str | None = None,
        project_id: str | None = None,
        limit: int = 100,
    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Query events from the event store (newest first).

        Events are immutable and are never modified after creation.

        Args:
            event_type: Filter by exact event type. Defaults to None.
            project_id: Filter by project identifier. Defaults to None.
            limit: Maximum number of events to return. Defaults to 100.

        Returns:
            list[dict[str, Any]]: List of event dictionaries with deserialized payloads.
        """
        with self._connect() as conn:
            sql = "SELECT * FROM events WHERE 1=1"
            params: list[Any] = []
            if event_type:
                sql += " AND type = ?"
                params.append(event_type)
            if project_id:
                sql += " AND project_id = ?"
                params.append(project_id)
            sql += " ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?"
            params.append(limit)
            rows = conn.execute(sql, params).fetchall()
            result = []
            for r in rows:
                d = dict(r)
                try:
                    d["payload"] = json.loads(d["payload"])
                except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError) as e:
                    logger.warning("Failed to deserialize payload: %s", e)
                result.append(d)
            return result

def test_handle_event_failure_records_event(self, tmp_path):
        """An exception from handle_event is recorded as a HookFailure event
        and re-raised so the CLI exits non-zero."""
        repo = tmp_path / "repo"
        repo.mkdir()
        db = tmp_path / "runtime.db"
        runner = CliRunner()
        runner.invoke(cli, ["--db", str(db), "--repo", str(repo), "init"])

        # Force handle_event to raise by patching the coordinator method.
        with mock.patch(
            "cogz.lifecycle.coordinator.LifecycleCoordinator.handle_event",
            side_effect=RuntimeError("simulated capture failure"),
        ):
            result = runner.invoke(cli, [
                "--db", str(db),
                "--repo", str(repo),
                "capture-event",
                "--agent", "devin",
                "--event", "SessionStart",
                "--payload", json.dumps({"session_id": "s1"}),
            ])

        assert result.exit_code != 0
        # The exception is re-raised; CliRunner stores it on result.exception.
        assert isinstance(result.exception, RuntimeError)
        assert "simulated capture failure" in str(result.exception)

        # A HookFailure event must have been recorded.
        from cogz.storage import Storage
        storage = Storage(db)
        events = storage.query_events(event_type="HookFailure", limit=100)
        assert len(events) >= 1
        payload = events[0]["payload"]
        assert payload["event"] == "SessionStart"
        assert "simulated capture failure" in payload["error"]

def run_code_context(adapter: BenchmarkAdapter, *, mode: str = "in_process", baseline: str = "full_cogz", seed: int = 42) -> BenchmarkResult:
    spec = SCENARIOS["code-context"]
    adapter = apply_baseline(adapter, baseline)
    result = _base_result(spec, mode, baseline, seed)
    env = _gate_env(result)
    trace = ToolTrace()
    try:
        responses: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
        for operation, kwargs in (
            ("index_repository", {"mode": "incremental"}),
            ("search", {"query": "cache", "top_k": 10}),
            ("get_context", {"query": "cache", "limit": 10}),
            ("build_context_pack", {"pack_type": "repository", "target": "fixture-repo"}),
        ):
            event = trace.record(operation, kwargs)
            response = getattr(adapter, operation)(**kwargs)
            event.finish(result=response)
            responses[operation] = response

        search_resp = responses.get("search", {})
        search_result_texts = _extract_result_texts(search_resp)
        index_resp = responses.get("index_repository", {})

def test_held_out_cross_session_decision_recall(tmp_path: Path):
    """Cross-session: capture decisions, consolidate, retrieve in later session.

    Verifies that decisions captured in one session are persisted and
    retrievable after consolidation in a subsequent search/context call.
    """
    adapter = _setup_runtime(tmp_path)
    try:
        result = run_lifecycle_scenario("cross-session", adapter, mode="in_process")
        assert result.passed, f"Scenario failed: {result.errors}"
        assert len(result.tool_trace) > 0, "No operations were executed"
        # Scenario gates (not runner-added) must carry in_process provenance
        scenario_gates = [g for g in result.gates if g.execution_surface]
        for gate in scenario_gates:
            assert gate.execution_surface == "in_process", f"Gate {gate.name} has wrong surface: {gate.execution_surface}"
        # Capture persistence gate must have real numerator/denominator
        persistence = next(g for g in result.gates if g.name == "capture_persistence")
        assert persistence.numerator is not None, "Capture persistence gate has no numerator"
        assert persistence.denominator is not None, "Capture persistence gate has no denominator"
        # Consolidation must have completed without errors
        consolidation = next(g for g in result.gates if g.name == "consolidation_completed")
        assert consolidation.passed, "Consolidation failed"
    finally:
        adapter.state.close()

"""Graph algorithm library for CogZ.

Pure Python implementations of graph algorithms for architectural analysis.
No external dependencies (NetworkX, igraph, etc.) at runtime.

Target scale: 1K-10K nodes, 2K-20K edges.
All algorithms load the graph into an in-memory adjacency list, run, and

def _fetch_entities_for_reindex(
        self,
        storage: Any,
        etype: str,
        spec: EntitySpec,
        project: str | None,
    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Fetch entities from storage for reindexing.

        For "node" entity type with code model, filters to only code node
        types (Function, Class, File, etc.). Knowledge entries stored as
        nodes are excluded — they have their own table entries with bge-base
        embeddings. Also fetches consolidation_status for vec_entities sync.
        """
        from .constants import CODE_ENTITY_TYPES, CODE_NODE_TYPES

        is_code = etype in CODE_ENTITY_TYPES
        table = spec.table
        text_expr = spec.text_expr
        proj_col = spec.project_col

        with storage._connect() as conn:
            status_expr = "consolidation_status" if "consolidation_status" in [
                row["name"] for row in conn.execute(f"PRAGMA table_info({table})").fetchall()
            ] else "'active' as consolidation_status"
            if etype == "node" and is_code:
                placeholders = ", ".join(["?"] * len(CODE_NODE_TYPES))
                sql = f"SELECT id, {text_expr} as text, {proj_col} as project, subcategory, domain, {status_expr} FROM {table} WHERE type IN ({placeholders})"
                params: list[Any] = list(CODE_NODE_TYPES)
                if project:
                    sql += f" AND {proj_col} = ?"
                    params.append(project)
            else:
                sql = f"SELECT id, {text_expr} as text, {proj_col} as project, subcategory, domain, {status_expr} FROM {table}"
                params = []
                if project:
                    sql += f" WHERE {proj_col} = ?"
                    params.append(project)
            rows = conn.execute(sql, params).fetchall()
            return [dict(r) for r in rows if r["text"]]

def pagerank(
        self,
        edge_types: list[str] | None = None,
        project_id: str | None = None,
        damping: float = 0.85,
        max_iter: int = 20,
        tol: float = 1e-6,
    ) -> dict[str, float]:
        """Compute PageRank with dangling node handling.

        High PageRank = architecturally significant, widely depended upon.
        Dangling nodes (no outgoing edges) redistribute rank uniformly.

        Args:
            edge_types: Edge types to consider. Defaults to dependency edges.
            project_id: Filter to specific project.
            damping: Damping factor (default 0.85).
            max_iter: Maximum iterations (default 20 per roadmap).
            tol: Convergence tolerance (L1 norm).

        Returns:
            {node_id: pagerank_score}. Scores sum to ~1.0.
        """
        if edge_types is None:
            edge_types = list(DEPENDENCY_EDGE_TYPES)
        adj = self._load_adjacency(edge_types=edge_types, project_id=project_id)

        nodes = set(adj.keys())
        for neighbors in adj.values():
            nodes.update(neighbors)
        n = len(nodes)
        if n == 0:
            return {}

        # Build reverse adjacency for efficient incoming lookup
        reverse: dict[str, list[str]] = {v: [] for v in nodes}
        for v, neighbors in adj.items():
            for w in neighbors:
                reverse[w].append(v)
