sections.title: _resolve_symbol
sections.content:
def _resolve_symbol(self, name: str, current_file: dict[str, Any],
                        cross_file_symbols: dict[tuple[str, str], str],
                        global_symbols: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> str | None:
        """Resolve a symbol name to a node ID via the cross-file symbol index.

        Resolution order (hierarchical):
        1. Same directory (O(1) dict lookup)
        2. Parent directory, grandparent, etc. (walk up the tree)
        3. Global fallback (name -> node_id) for cross-tree imports

        This replaces the old O(n²) iteration through all files and
        fixes resolution for symbols in parent/sibling directories.
        """
        # Guard against empty/malformed paths
        if not current_file.get("path"):
            return None
        current_dir = str(Path(current_file["path"]).parent)
        # 1. Same directory
        node_id = cross_file_symbols.get((current_dir, name))
        if node_id:
            return node_id
        # 2. Walk up parent directories
        parent = str(Path(current_dir).parent)
        while parent != current_dir:
            node_id = cross_file_symbols.get((parent, name))
            if node_id:
                return node_id
            current_dir = parent
            parent = str(Path(current_dir).parent)
        # 3. Global fallback
        if global_symbols:
            return global_symbols.get(name)
        return None

def _predict(self, text_a: str, text_b: str) -> dict[str, float] | None:
        """Run NLI classification on a text pair.

        Returns dict with keys 'entailment', 'neutral', 'contradiction'
        mapping to probabilities (0.0-1.0), or None if model unavailable.

        Includes a string equality fast-path: if the canonical forms of
        both texts are identical, returns entailment with high confidence
        without calling the model. This avoids the known NLI failure mode
        where small models classify identical texts as "neutral".
        """
        # Fast-path: identical texts are always entailment
        canonical_a = " ".join(text_a.lower().split())
        canonical_b = " ".join(text_b.lower().split())
        if canonical_a == canonical_b:
            return {"entailment": 0.99, "neutral": 0.005, "contradiction": 0.005}

        self._check_idle_ttl()
        self._load_model()
        if not self._loaded:
            return None
        self._last_used = time.time()

        try:
            # ONNX backend returns logits
            scores = self._model.predict([(text_a, text_b)])
            # Softmax to convert logits to probabilities
            if hasattr(scores, 'tolist'):
                scores = scores.tolist()
            elif hasattr(scores, '__iter__'):

            else:

def parse_header(content: str) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], str]:
    """Parse metadata header from file content.

    Returns (metadata_dict, body_content).
    """
    metadata: dict[str, Any] = {}

    # Try new 3-line format. The provenance line accepts an optional
    # legacy "tier=X " prefix for backward compatibility.
    new_pattern = re.compile(
        r"<!-- cogz:id=(\S+) type=(\S+) format=(\S+) version=(\d+) -->\n"
        r"<!-- cogz:provenance (?:tier=\S+ )?model=(\S+) source_rule=(\S+) -->\n"
        r"<!-- cogz:content_hash=(\S+) created_at=(\S+) updated_at=(\S+) author=(.+?) -->\n"
    )
    match = new_pattern.match(content)
    if match:
        metadata["id"] = match.group(1)
        metadata["type"] = match.group(2)
        metadata["format"] = match.group(3)
        metadata["version"] = int(match.group(4))
        metadata["model"] = match.group(5)
        metadata["source_rule"] = match.group(6)
        metadata["content_hash"] = match.group(7)
        metadata["created_at"] = match.group(8)
        metadata["updated_at"] = match.group(9)
        metadata["author"] = match.group(10)
        return metadata, content[match.end():]

    # Fall back to old single-line format
    old_pattern = re.compile(
        r"<!-- cogz:id=(\S+) type=(\S+) format=(\S+)(?: title=(.*?))? -->\n"
    )
    match = old_pattern.match(content)
    if match:
        metadata["id"] = match.group(1)
        metadata["type"] = match.group(2)
        metadata["format"] = match.group(3)
        if match.group(4):

sections.content:
def _fetch_entities_for_reindex(
        self,
        storage: Any,
        etype: str,
        spec: EntitySpec,
        project: str | None,
    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Fetch entities from storage for reindexing.

        For "node" entity type with code model, filters to only code node
        types (Function, Class, File, etc.). Knowledge entries stored as
        nodes are excluded — they have their own table entries with bge-base
        embeddings. Also fetches consolidation_status for vec_entities sync.
        """
        from .constants import CODE_ENTITY_TYPES, CODE_NODE_TYPES

        is_code = etype in CODE_ENTITY_TYPES
        table = spec.table
        text_expr = spec.text_expr
        proj_col = spec.project_col

        with storage._connect() as conn:
            status_expr = "consolidation_status" if "consolidation_status" in [
                row["name"] for row in conn.execute(f"PRAGMA table_info({table})").fetchall()
            ] else "'active' as consolidation_status"
            if etype == "node" and is_code:
                placeholders = ", ".join(["?"] * len(CODE_NODE_TYPES))
                sql = f"SELECT id, {text_expr} as text, {proj_col} as project, subcategory, domain, {status_expr} FROM {table} WHERE type IN ({placeholders})"
                params: list[Any] = list(CODE_NODE_TYPES)
                if project:
                    sql += f" AND {proj_col} = ?"
                    params.append(project)
            else:
                sql = f"SELECT id, {text_expr} as text, {proj_col} as project, subcategory, domain, {status_expr} FROM {table}"
                params = []
                if project:
                    sql += f" WHERE {proj_col} = ?"
                    params.append(project)
            rows = conn.execute(sql, params).fetchall()
            return [dict(r) for r in rows if r["text"]]

def _extract_signature(node, source: bytes) -> str:
    """Extract the function/class signature from a tree-sitter node.

    Returns the def/class line including decorators, name, parameters,
    and return type annotation (if present). The signature is the first
    line(s) up to the colon that starts the body.
    """
    # For function_definition: include decorators + def line
    # For class_definition: include decorators + class line
    start_byte = node.start_byte
    # Find the body node to get the end of the signature
    body = node.child_by_field_name("body")
    if body:
        end_byte = body.start_byte
    else:
        # Fallback: find the colon
        text = source[start_byte:node.end_byte].decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
        colon_idx = text.find(":")
        if colon_idx >= 0:
            return text[:colon_idx + 1].strip()
        return text.strip()

    sig = source[start_byte:end_byte].decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    # Clean up: collapse whitespace, strip trailing colon
    sig = " ".join(sig.split())
    if not sig.endswith(":"):
        sig += ":"
    return sig

def _fix_consolidation_lineage(self, issues: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> int:
        """Remove orphaned supersedes edges."""
        fixed = 0
        with self.storage._connect() as conn:
            for issue in issues:

                if edge_id:
                    conn.execute("DELETE FROM edges WHERE id = ?", (edge_id,))
                    fixed += 1
            conn.commit()
        return fixed

def prune_telemetry(self, retention_days: int | None = None) -> int:
        """Delete telemetry entries older than the retention period.

        Args:
            retention_days: Override TELEMETRY_RETENTION_DAYS. If None, uses the constant.

        Returns:
            Number of entries deleted.
        """
        from .constants import TELEMETRY_RETENTION_DAYS
        days = retention_days if retention_days is not None else TELEMETRY_RETENTION_DAYS
        with self._connect() as conn:
            cursor = conn.execute(
                "DELETE FROM telemetry "
                "WHERE created_at < datetime('now', ?)",
                (f"-{days} days",),
            )
            if not self._in_transaction:
                conn.commit()
            return cursor.rowcount

def record_telemetry(
        self,
        event_type: str,
        payload: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        project_id: str | None = None,
    ) -> str:
        """Record a telemetry event for analysis and tuning.

        No-op when COGZ_TELEMETRY_ENABLED is false (zero overhead).

        Args:
            event_type: Telemetry event type (e.g., search_query, consolidation_dedup).
            payload: Event-specific data dict (JSON-serialized).
            project_id: Optional project scope.

        Returns:
            The telemetry entry ID, or "" if telemetry is disabled.
        """
        from .constants import TELEMETRY_ENABLED
        if not TELEMETRY_ENABLED:
            # Also check config store (may be enabled via `cogz config set`)
            if self._config_store is not None:
                if not self._config_store.get("telemetry.enabled", False):
                    return ""
            else:
                return ""
        eid = make_id()
        resolved_project_id = project_id if project_id is not None else self.project_id
        with self._connect() as conn:
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO telemetry (id, event_type, payload, project_id, created_at) "
                "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (eid, event_type, json.dumps(payload or {}), resolved_project_id, now_iso()),
            )
            if not self._in_transaction:
                conn.commit()
        return eid

def delete_node(self, node_id: str) -> bool:
        """Delete a node by its unique identifier.

        Args:
            node_id: The unique identifier of the node to delete.

        Returns:
            bool: True if the node was deleted, False if not found.

        with self._connect() as conn:

        if result:

"""Consolidation engine for CogZ (Phase 2).

Deduplicates, merges, and detects contradictions in observations,
rules, and knowledge — keeping memory clean and accurate over time.

All consolidation operations are taxonomy-scoped: dedup and
contradiction detection only compare entities within the same
(project, subcategory) scope, preventing false positives from
cross-project comparisons.

Phases:
  A: Semantic Dedup Scan (fingerprint → embedding cosine → NLI entailment)
  B: Mechanical Merge (line-union, mark superseded, create graph edges)
  C: Contradiction Detection (NLI scoring, record as observations, flag contested)
  D: Temporal Validity Update (set valid_from/valid_until)
  E: Stale Knowledge Detection (importance decay, flag for review)
  F: Cross-Category Weave (optional, opt-in — cross-subcategory edges)
  G: Cross-Domain Synthesize (optional, manual — LLM-assisted insight generation)

Protection filters (Phase B only):
  - consolidation_locked entities are never merged
  - VALIDATED rules (lifecycle status in properties JSON) are protected
  - Knowledge promoted from rules (canonical) is protected
  - Entities with importance >= CONSOLIDATION_PROTECT_IMPORTANCE are protected

Phase C still runs on protected entities but flags them for review
instead of auto-superseding.
"""

def test_prune(self, tmp_db, monkeypatch):
        """prune_telemetry deletes old entries."""
        import cogz.constants as const
        monkeypatch.setattr(const, "TELEMETRY_ENABLED", True)

        # Insert a current entry
        tmp_db.record_telemetry("search_query", {"q": "current"})

        # Insert an old entry directly (bypass the enabled check)
        import json

        from cogz.storage import make_id
        old_time = "2020-01-01T00:00:00+00:00"
        with tmp_db._connect() as conn:
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO telemetry (id, event_type, payload, project_id, created_at) "
                "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (make_id(), "search_query", json.dumps({"q": "old"}), None, old_time),
            )
            conn.commit()

        # Prune with 30-day retention — should delete the old entry
        deleted = tmp_db.prune_telemetry(retention_days=30)
        assert deleted == 1

        rows = tmp_db.query_telemetry(limit=100)
        assert len(rows) == 1
        assert rows[0]["payload"]["q"] == "current"

def prune_telemetry(self, retention_days: int | None = None) -> int:
        """Delete telemetry entries older than the retention period.

        Args:
            retention_days: Override TELEMETRY_RETENTION_DAYS. If None, uses the constant.

        Returns:
            Number of entries deleted.
        """
        from .constants import TELEMETRY_RETENTION_DAYS
        days = retention_days if retention_days is not None else TELEMETRY_RETENTION_DAYS
        with self._connect() as conn:
            cursor = conn.execute(
                "DELETE FROM telemetry "
                "WHERE created_at < datetime('now', ?)",
                (f"-{days} days",),
            )
            if not self._in_transaction:
                conn.commit()
            return cursor.rowcount

def record_telemetry(
        self,
        event_type: str,
        payload: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        project_id: str | None = None,
    ) -> str:
        """Record a telemetry event for analysis and tuning.

        No-op when COGZ_TELEMETRY_ENABLED is false (zero overhead).

        Args:
            event_type: Telemetry event type (e.g., search_query, consolidation_dedup).
            payload: Event-specific data dict (JSON-serialized).
            project_id: Optional project scope.

        Returns:
            The telemetry entry ID, or "" if telemetry is disabled.
        """
        from .constants import TELEMETRY_ENABLED
        if not TELEMETRY_ENABLED:
            # Also check config store (may be enabled via `cogz config set`)
            if self._config_store is not None:
                if not self._config_store.get("telemetry.enabled", False):
                    return ""
            else:
                return ""
        eid = make_id()
        resolved_project_id = project_id if project_id is not None else self.project_id
        with self._connect() as conn:
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO telemetry (id, event_type, payload, project_id, created_at) "
                "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (eid, event_type, json.dumps(payload or {}), resolved_project_id, now_iso()),
            )
            if not self._in_transaction:
                conn.commit()
        return eid

def _rebuild_fts_nodes_if_needed(self, conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
        """Rebuild fts_nodes FTS5 table if searchable_text or type column is missing.

        FTS5 virtual tables can't be ALTERed — must drop and recreate.
        """
        fts_cols = conn.execute("PRAGMA table_info(fts_nodes)").fetchall()
        fts_col_names = {row["name"] for row in fts_cols} if fts_cols else set()
        if "searchable_text" not in fts_col_names or "type" not in fts_col_names:
            conn.execute("DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS fts_nodes_ai")
            conn.execute("DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS fts_nodes_ad")
            conn.execute("DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS fts_nodes_au")
            conn.execute("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS fts_nodes")
            conn.execute(
                "CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE fts_nodes USING fts5("
                "label, searchable_text, type UNINDEXED, "
                "project_id UNINDEXED, subcategory UNINDEXED, domain UNINDEXED, "
                "content='nodes', content_rowid='rowid', "
                "tokenize='porter unicode61 remove_diacritics 1')"
            )
            conn.execute(
                "CREATE TRIGGER fts_nodes_ai AFTER INSERT ON nodes BEGIN "
                "INSERT INTO fts_nodes(rowid, label, searchable_text, type, project_id, subcategory, domain) "
                "VALUES (new.rowid, new.label, new.searchable_text, new.type, new.project_id, new.subcategory, new.domain); END"
            )
            conn.execute(
                "CREATE TRIGGER fts_nodes_ad AFTER DELETE ON nodes BEGIN "
                "INSERT INTO fts_nodes(fts_nodes, rowid, label, searchable_text, type, project_id, subcategory, domain) "
                "VALUES ('delete', old.rowid, old.label, old.searchable_text, old.type, old.project_id, old.subcategory, old.domain); END"
            )
            conn.execute(
                "CREATE TRIGGER fts_nodes_au AFTER UPDATE ON nodes BEGIN "
                "INSERT INTO fts_nodes(fts_nodes, rowid, label, searchable_text, type, project_id, subcategory, domain) "
                "VALUES ('delete', old.rowid, old.label, old.searchable_text, old.type, old.project_id, old.subcategory, old.domain); "
                "INSERT INTO fts_nodes(rowid, label, searchable_text, type, project_id, subcategory, domain) "

def _extract_signature(node, source: bytes) -> str:
    """Extract the function/class signature from a tree-sitter node.

    Returns the def/class line including decorators, name, parameters,
    and return type annotation (if present). The signature is the first
    line(s) up to the colon that starts the body.
    """
    # For function_definition: include decorators + def line
    # For class_definition: include decorators + class line
    start_byte = node.start_byte
    # Find the body node to get the end of the signature
    body = node.child_by_field_name("body")
    if body:
        end_byte = body.start_byte
    else:
        # Fallback: find the colon
        text = source[start_byte:node.end_byte].decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
        colon_idx = text.find(":")
        if colon_idx >= 0:
            return text[:colon_idx + 1].strip()
        return text.strip()

    sig = source[start_byte:end_byte].decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    # Clean up: collapse whitespace, strip trailing colon
    sig = " ".join(sig.split())
    if not sig.endswith(":"):
        sig += ":"
    return sig

def _collect_file_learning_context(
        self,
        file_name: str,
        learning_kwargs: dict[str, Any],
        content: dict[str, Any],
        sources: list[dict[str, Any]],
    ) -> None:
        """Collect learning entities (observations, patterns, rules) mentioning a file."""
        if self.learning is None:
            return
        obs = sorted(self.learning.query_observations(**learning_kwargs), key=lambda e: e.get("created_at", ""), reverse=True)
        file_obs = [o for o in obs if file_name.lower() in o.get("statement", "").lower()]
        if file_obs:
            content["related_observations"] = [o["statement"] for o in file_obs[:5]]
            sources.append({"type": "learning", "query": "observations mentioning file", "count": len(file_obs)})

        # Patterns and rules relevant to this file
        patterns = sorted(self.learning.query_patterns(**learning_kwargs), key=lambda e: e.get("created_at", ""), reverse=True)
        file_patterns = [p["statement"] for p in patterns if file_name.lower() in p.get("statement", "").lower() or any(file_name.lower() in obs_id.lower() for obs_id in p.get("supporting_observation_ids", []))][:5]
        if file_patterns:
            content["relevant_patterns"] = file_patterns
            sources.append({"type": "learning", "query": "patterns mentioning file", "count": len(file_patterns)})

        rules = sorted(self.learning.query_rules(**learning_kwargs), key=lambda e: e.get("created_at", ""), reverse=True)
        validated = [r for r in rules if r.get("properties", {}).get("status") == "VALIDATED"]
        file_rules = [r["statement"] for r in validated if file_name.lower() in r.get("statement", "").lower()][:5]
        if file_rules:
            content["relevant_rules"] = file_rules
            sources.append({"type": "learning", "query": "rules mentioning file", "count": len(file_rules)})

sections.content:
def _extract_signature(node, source: bytes) -> str:
    """Extract the function/class signature from a tree-sitter node.

    Returns the def/class line including decorators, name, parameters,
    and return type annotation (if present). The signature is the first
    line(s) up to the colon that starts the body.
    """
    # For function_definition: include decorators + def line
    # For class_definition: include decorators + class line
    start_byte = node.start_byte
    # Find the body node to get the end of the signature
    body = node.child_by_field_name("body")
    if body:
        end_byte = body.start_byte
    else:
        # Fallback: find the colon
        text = source[start_byte:node.end_byte].decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
        colon_idx = text.find(":")
        if colon_idx >= 0:
            return text[:colon_idx + 1].strip()
        return text.strip()

    sig = source[start_byte:end_byte].decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    # Clean up: collapse whitespace, strip trailing colon
    sig = " ".join(sig.split())
    if not sig.endswith(":"):
        sig += ":"
    return sig

def _predict(self, text_a: str, text_b: str) -> dict[str, float] | None:
        """Run NLI classification on a text pair.

        Returns dict with keys 'entailment', 'neutral', 'contradiction'
        mapping to probabilities (0.0-1.0), or None if model unavailable.

        Includes a string equality fast-path: if the canonical forms of
        both texts are identical, returns entailment with high confidence
        without calling the model. This avoids the known NLI failure mode
        where small models classify identical texts as "neutral".
        """
        # Fast-path: identical texts are always entailment
        canonical_a = " ".join(text_a.lower().split())
        canonical_b = " ".join(text_b.lower().split())
        if canonical_a == canonical_b:
            return {"entailment": 0.99, "neutral": 0.005, "contradiction": 0.005}

        self._check_idle_ttl()
        self._load_model()
        if not self._loaded:
            return None
        self._last_used = time.time()

        try:
            # ONNX backend returns logits
            scores = self._model.predict([(text_a, text_b)])
            # Softmax to convert logits to probabilities
            if hasattr(scores, 'tolist'):
                scores = scores.tolist()
            elif hasattr(scores, '__iter__'):
                scores = list(scores)
            else:
                scores = [float(scores)]

            # Handle nested list shape: [[s0, s1, s2]]
            if scores and isinstance(scores[0], list):
                scores = scores[0]

    spec = SCENARIOS["code-context"]
    adapter = apply_baseline(adapter, baseline)
    result = _base_result(spec, mode, baseline, seed)
    env = _gate_env(result)
    trace = ToolTrace()
    try:
        responses: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
        for operation, kwargs in (
            ("index_repository", {"mode": "incremental"}),
            ("search", {"query": "cache", "top_k": 10}),
            ("get_context", {"query": "cache", "limit": 10}),
            ("build_context_pack", {"pack_type": "repository", "target": "fixture-repo"}),
        ):
            event = trace.record(operation, kwargs)
            response = getattr(adapter, operation)(**kwargs)
            event.finish(result=response)
            responses[operation] = response

        search_resp = responses.get("search", {})
        search_result_texts = _extract_result_texts(search_resp)
        index_resp = responses.get("index_repository", {})
        context_resp = responses.get("get_context", {})
        pack_resp = responses.get("build_context_pack", {})

        stats = index_resp.get("stats", {}) if isinstance(index_resp, dict) else {}
        search_result_ids = _extract_result_ids(search_resp)
        result.metrics["operations_completed"] = len(trace.events)
        result.metrics["indexed_files"] = stats.get("indexed", stats.get("files_indexed", stats.get("total", 0))) if isinstance(stats, dict) else 0

def _predict(self, text_a: str, text_b: str) -> dict[str, float] | None:
        """Run NLI classification on a text pair.

        Returns dict with keys 'entailment', 'neutral', 'contradiction'
        mapping to probabilities (0.0-1.0), or None if model unavailable.

        Includes a string equality fast-path: if the canonical forms of
        both texts are identical, returns entailment with high confidence
        without calling the model. This avoids the known NLI failure mode
        where small models classify identical texts as "neutral".
        """
        # Fast-path: identical texts are always entailment
        canonical_a = " ".join(text_a.lower().split())
        canonical_b = " ".join(text_b.lower().split())
        if canonical_a == canonical_b:
            return {"entailment": 0.99, "neutral": 0.005, "contradiction": 0.005}

        self._check_idle_ttl()
        self._load_model()
        if not self._loaded:
            return None
        self._last_used = time.time()

        try:
            # ONNX backend returns logits
            scores = self._model.predict([(text_a, text_b)])
            # Softmax to convert logits to probabilities
            if hasattr(scores, 'tolist'):
                scores = scores.tolist()
            elif hasattr(scores, '__iter__'):
                scores = list(scores)
            else:
                scores = [float(scores)]

            # Handle nested list shape: [[s0, s1, s2]]
            if scores and isinstance(scores[0], list):

            # Apply softmax

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Iterable
from typing import Any

from .base import BenchmarkAdapter


class HookReplayAdapter:
    """Small adapter for deterministic hook event replay scenarios."""

    def __init__(self, delegate: BenchmarkAdapter):
        self.delegate = delegate

    def replay(self, events: Iterable[dict[str, Any]], **scope: Any) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        results = []
        for item in events:
            results.append(
                self.delegate.capture_event(
                    item.get("agent", "fixture-agent"),
                    item["event"],
                    item.get("payload", {}),
                    **scope,
                )
            )
        return results

sections.title: _resolve_symbol
sections.content:
def _resolve_symbol(self, name: str, current_file: dict[str, Any],
                        cross_file_symbols: dict[tuple[str, str], str],
                        global_symbols: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> str | None:
        """Resolve a symbol name to a node ID via the cross-file symbol index.

        Resolution order (hierarchical):
        1. Same directory (O(1) dict lookup)
        2. Parent directory, grandparent, etc. (walk up the tree)
        3. Global fallback (name -> node_id) for cross-tree imports

        This replaces the old O(n²) iteration through all files and
        fixes resolution for symbols in parent/sibling directories.
        """
        # Guard against empty/malformed paths
        if not current_file.get("path"):
            return None
        current_dir = str(Path(current_file["path"]).parent)
        # 1. Same directory
        node_id = cross_file_symbols.get((current_dir, name))
        if node_id:
            return node_id
        # 2. Walk up parent directories
        parent = str(Path(current_dir).parent)
        while parent != current_dir:
            node_id = cross_file_symbols.get((parent, name))
            if node_id:
                return node_id
            current_dir = parent
            parent = str(Path(current_dir).parent)
        # 3. Global fallback
        if global_symbols:
            return global_symbols.get(name)
        return None

def _predict(self, text_a: str, text_b: str) -> dict[str, float] | None:
        """Run NLI classification on a text pair.

        Returns dict with keys 'entailment', 'neutral', 'contradiction'
        mapping to probabilities (0.0-1.0), or None if model unavailable.

        Includes a string equality fast-path: if the canonical forms of
        both texts are identical, returns entailment with high confidence
        without calling the model. This avoids the known NLI failure mode
        where small models classify identical texts as "neutral".
        """
        # Fast-path: identical texts are always entailment
        canonical_a = " ".join(text_a.lower().split())
        canonical_b = " ".join(text_b.lower().split())
        if canonical_a == canonical_b:
            return {"entailment": 0.99, "neutral": 0.005, "contradiction": 0.005}

        self._check_idle_ttl()
        self._load_model()
        if not self._loaded:
            return None
        self._last_used = time.time()

        try:
            # ONNX backend returns logits
            scores = self._model.predict([(text_a, text_b)])
            # Softmax to convert logits to probabilities
            if hasattr(scores, 'tolist'):
                scores = scores.tolist()
            elif hasattr(scores, '__iter__'):
                scores = list(scores)
            else:
                scores = [float(scores)]

            # Handle nested list shape: [[s0, s1, s2]]
            if scores and isinstance(scores[0], list):

def test_migrations_are_atomic_on_failure(tmp_path):
    """If a migration fails mid-way, earlier migrations in the same
    transaction should be rolled back — no partial state.

    This tests the transaction pattern used in _ensure_db: all ALTER TABLE
    migrations run inside a single BEGIN/commit block, so a failure on any
    migration rolls back all prior migrations in the same batch.
    """
    import sqlite3

    db_path = tmp_path / "runtime_fail.db"
    s = Storage(db_path)
    s.close()

    # Remove the 'format' column from knowledge by recreating without it
    with sqlite3.connect(db_path) as conn:
        cols = [r[1] for r in conn.execute("PRAGMA table_info(knowledge)").fetchall()]
        cols_no_format = [c for c in cols if c != "format"]
        col_list = ", ".join(cols_no_format)
        conn.execute("ALTER TABLE knowledge RENAME TO knowledge_old")
        create_cols = ", ".join(cols_no_format)
        conn.execute(f"CREATE TABLE knowledge ({create_cols})")
        conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO knowledge ({col_list}) SELECT {col_list} FROM knowledge_old")
        conn.execute("DROP TABLE knowledge_old")
        conn.commit()

    # Simulate the migration transaction pattern from _ensure_db:
    # BEGIN, run valid migration, run invalid migration, rollback on failure
    # Use sqlite3 directly to avoid Storage re-running migrations
    with sqlite3.connect(db_path) as conn:
        conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        cols_before = [r["name"] for r in conn.execute("PRAGMA table_info(knowledge)").fetchall()]
        assert "format" not in cols_before

        conn.execute("BEGIN")
        try:
            conn.execute("ALTER TABLE knowledge ADD COLUMN format TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'markdown'")
            # This will fail — table doesn't exist
            conn.execute("ALTER TABLE nonexistent_table ADD COLUMN foo TEXT")
            conn.commit()

def _predict(self, text_a: str, text_b: str) -> dict[str, float] | None:
        """Run NLI classification on a text pair.

        Returns dict with keys 'entailment', 'neutral', 'contradiction'
        mapping to probabilities (0.0-1.0), or None if model unavailable.

        Includes a string equality fast-path: if the canonical forms of
        both texts are identical, returns entailment with high confidence
        without calling the model. This avoids the known NLI failure mode
        where small models classify identical texts as "neutral".
        """
        # Fast-path: identical texts are always entailment
        canonical_a = " ".join(text_a.lower().split())
        canonical_b = " ".join(text_b.lower().split())
        if canonical_a == canonical_b:
            return {"entailment": 0.99, "neutral": 0.005, "contradiction": 0.005}

        self._check_idle_ttl()
        self._load_model()
        if not self._loaded:
            return None
        self._last_used = time.time()

        try:
            # ONNX backend returns logits
            scores = self._model.predict([(text_a, text_b)])
            # Softmax to convert logits to probabilities
            if hasattr(scores, 'tolist'):
                scores = scores.tolist()
            elif hasattr(scores, '__iter__'):
                scores = list(scores)
            else:
                scores = [float(scores)]

            # Handle nested list shape: [[s0, s1, s2]]

def _handle_contradiction(
        self,
        pair: ContradictionPair,
        etype: str,
        dry_run: bool,
        contested: list[tuple[str, str]],
        observations_created: int,
    ) -> int:
        """Handle a confirmed contradiction: record observation and flag entities.

        In dry_run mode, records what would be contested without writing.
        In real mode, creates a CONTRADICTION observation, flags entities as
        contested (or protected for review), and writes to the consolidation log.
        """
        if dry_run:
            # Preview: record what would be contested
            for eid in [pair.entity_a_id, pair.entity_b_id]:
                if self._is_protected(etype, eid):
                    pair.is_protected = True
                contested.append((etype, eid))
            return observations_created + 1

        # Record as a new observation
        obs_text = (
            f"Contradiction detected between {etype} {pair.entity_a_id} "
            f"and {etype} {pair.entity_b_id} "
            f"(cosine={pair.cosine_similarity:.3f}, "
            f"nli={pair.nli_contradiction_score})"
        )
        try:
            from .learning import LearningEngine
            learning = LearningEngine(self.storage)
            learning.create_observation(
                obs_text,
                source="consolidation",
                category="CONTRADICTION",
            )
            observations_created += 1
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning(f"Failed to record contradiction observation: {e}")

) -> GateResult:

    completed = consolidate_response.get("status") != "error" and not errors
    return GateResult(
        name="consolidation_completed",
        passed=completed,
        value=len(errors),
        threshold=0,
        message=f"Consolidation completed with {len(errors)} errors" + (f": {errors}" if errors else ""),
        numerator=0 if errors else 1,
        denominator=1,
        observed_ids=[],

        execution_surface=execution_surface,

    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s")

    all_results: list[ConsolidationResult] = []

    phases_to_run = {
        "dedup": bench_dedup,

        "pattern_rule": bench_pattern_rule_generation,
        "cross_category": bench_cross_category_weave,

    if phase:

            phases_to_run = {phase: phases_to_run[phase]}
        else:
            logger.error(f"Unknown phase: {phase}. Available: {list(phases_to_run.keys())}")
            return

    for phase_name, runner in phases_to_run.items():
        logger.info(f"\n{'='*60}")
        logger.info(f"Running consolidation phase: {phase_name}")
        logger.info(f"{'='*60}")
        try:
            results = runner()
            all_results.extend(results)

    json_data = [r.to_dict() for r in all_results]

def _predict(self, text_a: str, text_b: str) -> dict[str, float] | None:
        """Run NLI classification on a text pair.

        Returns dict with keys 'entailment', 'neutral', 'contradiction'
        mapping to probabilities (0.0-1.0), or None if model unavailable.

        Includes a string equality fast-path: if the canonical forms of
        both texts are identical, returns entailment with high confidence
        without calling the model. This avoids the known NLI failure mode
        where small models classify identical texts as "neutral".
        """
        # Fast-path: identical texts are always entailment
        canonical_a = " ".join(text_a.lower().split())
        canonical_b = " ".join(text_b.lower().split())
        if canonical_a == canonical_b:
            return {"entailment": 0.99, "neutral": 0.005, "contradiction": 0.005}

        self._check_idle_ttl()
        self._load_model()
        if not self._loaded:
            return None
        self._last_used = time.time()

        try:
            # ONNX backend returns logits
            scores = self._model.predict([(text_a, text_b)])
            # Softmax to convert logits to probabilities
            if hasattr(scores, 'tolist'):
                scores = scores.tolist()
            elif hasattr(scores, '__iter__'):
                scores = list(scores)
            else:
                scores = [float(scores)]

            # Handle nested list shape: [[s0, s1, s2]]
            if scores and isinstance(scores[0], list):

    return GateResult(
        name="consolidation_completed",

sections.title: _quality_rank_key
sections.content:
def _quality_rank_key(self, etype: str, entity: dict) -> tuple:
        """Compute a quality ranking key for canonical selection.

        Higher tuple = higher quality. Used to pick the canonical (winner)
        in dedup clusters. Ranking criteria (in priority order):
        1. Importance score (higher = better)
        2. Evidence count (more supporting entities = better)
        3. Confidence (for rules/patterns)
        4. Recency (newer = better, as tiebreaker)

        This implements the "best-of" selection from the cross-machine sync
        design: don't average conflicting interpretations — select the
        highest-quality one and supersede the rest.
        """
        eid = entity["entity_id"]
        importance = self.storage.get_importance(etype, eid)

        # Evidence count
        evidence_count = self._get_evidence_count(etype, eid)

        # Confidence (for rules/patterns)
        confidence = 0.0
        if etype in ("rule", "pattern"):
            entry = self.storage._query_one_raw(entity_table(etype), "id = ?", (eid,))
            if entry and entry.get("confidence") is not None:
                confidence = entry["confidence"]

        # Recency (ISO timestamp string — lexicographic sort works for ISO 8601)
        created = entity.get("created_at", "")

        return (importance, evidence_count, confidence, created)

def _predict(self, text_a: str, text_b: str) -> dict[str, float] | None:
        """Run NLI classification on a text pair.

        Returns dict with keys 'entailment', 'neutral', 'contradiction'
        mapping to probabilities (0.0-1.0), or None if model unavailable.

        Includes a string equality fast-path: if the canonical forms of
        both texts are identical, returns entailment with high confidence
        without calling the model. This avoids the known NLI failure mode
        where small models classify identical texts as "neutral".
        """
        # Fast-path: identical texts are always entailment
        canonical_a = " ".join(text_a.lower().split())
        canonical_b = " ".join(text_b.lower().split())
        if canonical_a == canonical_b:
            return {"entailment": 0.99, "neutral": 0.005, "contradiction": 0.005}

        self._check_idle_ttl()
        self._load_model()
        if not self._loaded:
            return None
        self._last_used = time.time()

        try:
            # ONNX backend returns logits
            scores = self._model.predict([(text_a, text_b)])
            # Softmax to convert logits to probabilities
            if hasattr(scores, 'tolist'):
                scores = scores.tolist()
            elif hasattr(scores, '__iter__'):
                scores = list(scores)
            else:
                scores = [float(scores)]

            # Handle nested list shape: [[s0, s1, s2]]
            if scores and isinstance(scores[0], list):

def test_update_preserves_consolidation_state_in_header(self, kl, tmp_repo_with_cogz):
        """update() writes consolidation state to file header for cross-machine sync."""
        kid = kl.create("architecture", "State Test", "Original content.", repo_path=tmp_repo_with_cogz)

        # Set consolidation state in DB
        kl.storage._update("knowledge", kid, {
            "consolidation_status": "superseded",
            "importance": 0.85,
            "consolidation_locked": 1,
        })

        # Update via API — force=True because the entry is consolidation_locked
        kl.update(kid, content="Updated content.", force=True)

        # Read the file and verify state line is present
        files = list((tmp_repo_with_cogz / ".cogz" / "knowledge" / "architecture").iterdir())
        assert len(files) == 1
        file_content = files[0].read_text()
        assert "cogz:state" in file_content
        assert "consolidation_status=superseded" in file_content
        assert "importance=0.85" in file_content

def _predict(self, text_a: str, text_b: str) -> dict[str, float] | None:
        """Run NLI classification on a text pair.

        Returns dict with keys 'entailment', 'neutral', 'contradiction'
        mapping to probabilities (0.0-1.0), or None if model unavailable.

        Includes a string equality fast-path: if the canonical forms of
        both texts are identical, returns entailment with high confidence
        without calling the model. This avoids the known NLI failure mode
        where small models classify identical texts as "neutral".
        """
        # Fast-path: identical texts are always entailment
        canonical_a = " ".join(text_a.lower().split())
        canonical_b = " ".join(text_b.lower().split())
        if canonical_a == canonical_b:
            return {"entailment": 0.99, "neutral": 0.005, "contradiction": 0.005}

        self._check_idle_ttl()
        self._load_model()
        if not self._loaded:
            return None
        self._last_used = time.time()

        try:
            # ONNX backend returns logits
            scores = self._model.predict([(text_a, text_b)])
            # Softmax to convert logits to probabilities
            if hasattr(scores, 'tolist'):
                scores = scores.tolist()
            elif hasattr(scores, '__iter__'):
                scores = list(scores)

def apply_fixes(self, checks: list[CheckResult] | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Apply safe repairs for fixable issues.

        Creates an automatic backup before applying any fixes.

        Args:
            checks: Optional list of CheckResults to fix. If None, runs all checks first.

        Returns:
            Dict with repair summary: {fixed: int, skipped: int, backup_path: str}
        """
        if checks is None:
            checks = self.run_all_checks()

        # Auto-backup before any repairs
        from .storage import now_iso
        backup_dir = self.storage.db_path.parent / "backups"
        backup_path = backup_dir / f"doctor-fix-{now_iso().replace(':', '-')}.db"
        try:
            self.storage.backup(backup_path)
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.warning(f"Backup before fixes failed: {exc}")  # Don't block fixes if backup fails

        fixed = 0
        skipped = 0
        details: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

        for check in checks:
            if not check.fixable or not check.issues:
                skipped += len(check.issues)
                continue

            if check.name == "graph_integrity":
                fixed_count = self._fix_graph_integrity(check.issues)
                fixed += fixed_count
                details.append({"check": check.name, "fixed": fixed_count})
            elif check.name == "consolidation_lineage":
                fixed_count = self._fix_consolidation_lineage(check.issues)

                details.append({"check": check.name, "fixed": fixed_count})

def apply_with_backup(
        self,
        operation: str,
        backup_dir: Path | None = None,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Execute a bulk operation with automatic backup.

        Args:
            operation: "rewrite", "retag", or "status".
            backup_dir: Directory for backup file. Defaults to storage's backup dir.
            **kwargs: Arguments for the bulk operation.

        Returns:
            Operation result dict (includes backup_path if backup was created).
        """
        if backup_dir is None:
            backup_dir = self.storage.db_path.parent / "backups"
        backup_path = backup_dir / f"bulk-{operation}-{now_iso().replace(':', '-')}.db"

        # Create backup before executing
        try:
            self.storage.backup(backup_path)
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.warning(f"Bulk operation backup failed: {exc}")
            backup_path = None

        # Execute with dry_run=False
        kwargs["dry_run"] = False
        if operation == "rewrite":
            result = self.bulk_rewrite(**kwargs)
        elif operation == "retag":
            result = self.bulk_retag(**kwargs)
        elif operation == "status":
            result = self.bulk_status(**kwargs)
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown operation: {operation}")

        result["backup_path"] = str(backup_path) if backup_path else None
        return result

def _predict(self, text_a: str, text_b: str) -> dict[str, float] | None:
        """Run NLI classification on a text pair.

        Returns dict with keys 'entailment', 'neutral', 'contradiction'
        mapping to probabilities (0.0-1.0), or None if model unavailable.

        Includes a string equality fast-path: if the canonical forms of
        both texts are identical, returns entailment with high confidence
        without calling the model. This avoids the known NLI failure mode
        where small models classify identical texts as "neutral".
        """
        # Fast-path: identical texts are always entailment
        canonical_a = " ".join(text_a.lower().split())
        canonical_b = " ".join(text_b.lower().split())
        if canonical_a == canonical_b:
            return {"entailment": 0.99, "neutral": 0.005, "contradiction": 0.005}

        self._check_idle_ttl()
        self._load_model()
        if not self._loaded:
            return None
        self._last_used = time.time()

        try:

            scores = self._model.predict([(text_a, text_b)])
            # Softmax to convert logits to probabilities
            if hasattr(scores, 'tolist'):
                scores = scores.tolist()
            elif hasattr(scores, '__iter__'):
                scores = list(scores)
            else:
                scores = [float(scores)]

def test_migrations_are_atomic_on_failure(tmp_path):
    """If a migration fails mid-way, earlier migrations in the same
    transaction should be rolled back — no partial state.

    This tests the transaction pattern used in _ensure_db: all ALTER TABLE
    migrations run inside a single BEGIN/commit block, so a failure on any
    migration rolls back all prior migrations in the same batch.
    """
    import sqlite3

    db_path = tmp_path / "runtime_fail.db"
    s = Storage(db_path)
    s.close()

    # Remove the 'format' column from knowledge by recreating without it
    with sqlite3.connect(db_path) as conn:
        cols = [r[1] for r in conn.execute("PRAGMA table_info(knowledge)").fetchall()]
        cols_no_format = [c for c in cols if c != "format"]
        col_list = ", ".join(cols_no_format)
        conn.execute("ALTER TABLE knowledge RENAME TO knowledge_old")
        create_cols = ", ".join(cols_no_format)
        conn.execute(f"CREATE TABLE knowledge ({create_cols})")
        conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO knowledge ({col_list}) SELECT {col_list} FROM knowledge_old")
        conn.execute("DROP TABLE knowledge_old")
        conn.commit()

    # Simulate the migration transaction pattern from _ensure_db:
    # BEGIN, run valid migration, run invalid migration, rollback on failure
    # Use sqlite3 directly to avoid Storage re-running migrations
    with sqlite3.connect(db_path) as conn:
        conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        cols_before = [r["name"] for r in conn.execute("PRAGMA table_info(knowledge)").fetchall()]
        assert "format" not in cols_before

    try:

            ("decision_made", {"decision": "use the repository cache", "rationale": "reduces repeated I/O"}),
            ("command_exec", {"command": "pytest tests/test_cache.py", "exit_code": 0}),
            ("session_end", {"summary": "Validated the cache design"}),
        ):
            resp = context.call(
                "capture_event",
                agent="fixture-agent",
                event=event,
                payload=payload,
                **context.scope,
            )
            capture_responses.append(resp)
            capture_payloads.append(payload)
        consolidate_resp = context.call("consolidate", **context.scope)
        auto_context_resp = context.call("get_auto_context", **context.scope)
        search_resp = context.call("search", query="cache", top_k=10, **context.scope)
        context_resp = context.call("get_context", query="cache", limit=10, **context.scope)

        relevant_ids = _relevant_ids_by_keyword(capture_responses, ["cache"], payloads=capture_payloads)

        result.metrics["operations_completed"] = len(context.trace.events)
        result.metrics["events_captured"] = len(captured_ids)
        result.metrics["search_results"] = len(search_result_ids)

def _predict(self, text_a: str, text_b: str) -> dict[str, float] | None:
        """Run NLI classification on a text pair.

        Returns dict with keys 'entailment', 'neutral', 'contradiction'
        mapping to probabilities (0.0-1.0), or None if model unavailable.

        Includes a string equality fast-path: if the canonical forms of
        both texts are identical, returns entailment with high confidence
        without calling the model. This avoids the known NLI failure mode
        where small models classify identical texts as "neutral".
        """
        # Fast-path: identical texts are always entailment
        canonical_a = " ".join(text_a.lower().split())
        canonical_b = " ".join(text_b.lower().split())
        if canonical_a == canonical_b:
            return {"entailment": 0.99, "neutral": 0.005, "contradiction": 0.005}

        self._check_idle_ttl()
        self._load_model()
        if not self._loaded:
            return None
        self._last_used = time.time()

        try:
            # ONNX backend returns logits
            scores = self._model.predict([(text_a, text_b)])
            # Softmax to convert logits to probabilities
            if hasattr(scores, 'tolist'):
                scores = scores.tolist()
            elif hasattr(scores, '__iter__'):
                scores = list(scores)
            else:
                scores = [float(scores)]

            # Handle nested list shape: [[s0, s1, s2]]
            if scores and isinstance(scores[0], list):

def _fetch_entities_for_reindex(
        self,
        storage: Any,
        etype: str,
        spec: EntitySpec,
        project: str | None,
    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Fetch entities from storage for reindexing.

        For "node" entity type with code model, filters to only code node
        types (Function, Class, File, etc.). Knowledge entries stored as
        nodes are excluded — they have their own table entries with bge-base
        embeddings. Also fetches consolidation_status for vec_entities sync.
        """
        from .constants import CODE_ENTITY_TYPES, CODE_NODE_TYPES

        is_code = etype in CODE_ENTITY_TYPES
        table = spec.table
        text_expr = spec.text_expr
        proj_col = spec.project_col

        with storage._connect() as conn:
            status_expr = "consolidation_status" if "consolidation_status" in [
                row["name"] for row in conn.execute(f"PRAGMA table_info({table})").fetchall()
            ] else "'active' as consolidation_status"
            if etype == "node" and is_code:
                placeholders = ", ".join(["?"] * len(CODE_NODE_TYPES))
                sql = f"SELECT id, {text_expr} as text, {proj_col} as project, subcategory, domain, {status_expr} FROM {table} WHERE type IN ({placeholders})"
                params: list[Any] = list(CODE_NODE_TYPES)
                if project:
                    sql += f" AND {proj_col} = ?"
                    params.append(project)
            else:
                sql = f"SELECT id, {text_expr} as text, {proj_col} as project, subcategory, domain, {status_expr} FROM {table}"
                params = []
                if project:
                    sql += f" WHERE {proj_col} = ?"
                    params.append(project)
            rows = conn.execute(sql, params).fetchall()
            return [dict(r) for r in rows if r["text"]]

def _predict(self, text_a: str, text_b: str) -> dict[str, float] | None:
        """Run NLI classification on a text pair.

        Returns dict with keys 'entailment', 'neutral', 'contradiction'
        mapping to probabilities (0.0-1.0), or None if model unavailable.

        Includes a string equality fast-path: if the canonical forms of
        both texts are identical, returns entailment with high confidence
        without calling the model. This avoids the known NLI failure mode
        where small models classify identical texts as "neutral".
        """
        # Fast-path: identical texts are always entailment
        canonical_a = " ".join(text_a.lower().split())
        canonical_b = " ".join(text_b.lower().split())
        if canonical_a == canonical_b:
            return {"entailment": 0.99, "neutral": 0.005, "contradiction": 0.005}

        self._check_idle_ttl()
        self._load_model()
        if not self._loaded:
            return None
        self._last_used = time.time()

        try:
            # ONNX backend returns logits
            scores = self._model.predict([(text_a, text_b)])
            # Softmax to convert logits to probabilities
            if hasattr(scores, 'tolist'):
                scores = scores.tolist()
            elif hasattr(scores, '__iter__'):
                scores = list(scores)
            else:
                scores = [float(scores)]

            # Handle nested list shape: [[s0, s1, s2]]
            if scores and isinstance(scores[0], list):
                scores = scores[0]

            # Apply softmax
            max_score = max(scores)

class HookReplayAdapter:
    """Small adapter for deterministic hook event replay scenarios."""

    def __init__(self, delegate: BenchmarkAdapter):
        self.delegate = delegate

    def replay(self, events: Iterable[dict[str, Any]], **scope: Any) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        results = []
        for item in events:
            results.append(

                    item["event"],
                    item.get("payload", {}),
                    **scope,

        project_id: str | None = None,
        damping: float = 0.85,
        max_iter: int = 20,
        tol: float = 1e-6,

        """Compute PageRank with dangling node handling.

        High PageRank = architecturally significant, widely depended upon.
        Dangling nodes (no outgoing edges) redistribute rank uniformly.

        Args:
            edge_types: Edge types to consider. Defaults to dependency edges.
            project_id: Filter to specific project.
            damping: Damping factor (default 0.85).
            max_iter: Maximum iterations (default 20 per roadmap).
            tol: Convergence tolerance (L1 norm).

        Returns:
            {node_id: pagerank_score}. Scores sum to ~1.0.
        """
        if edge_types is None:
            edge_types = list(DEPENDENCY_EDGE_TYPES)
        adj = self._load_adjacency(edge_types=edge_types, project_id=project_id)

        nodes = set(adj.keys())
        for neighbors in adj.values():
            nodes.update(neighbors)
        n = len(nodes)
        if n == 0:
            return {}

        # Build reverse adjacency for efficient incoming lookup
        reverse: dict[str, list[str]] = {v: [] for v in nodes}
        for v, neighbors in adj.items():
            for w in neighbors:
                reverse[w].append(v)

def _predict(self, text_a: str, text_b: str) -> dict[str, float] | None:
        """Run NLI classification on a text pair.

        Returns dict with keys 'entailment', 'neutral', 'contradiction'
        mapping to probabilities (0.0-1.0), or None if model unavailable.

        Includes a string equality fast-path: if the canonical forms of
        both texts are identical, returns entailment with high confidence
        without calling the model. This avoids the known NLI failure mode
        where small models classify identical texts as "neutral".
        """
        # Fast-path: identical texts are always entailment
        canonical_a = " ".join(text_a.lower().split())
        canonical_b = " ".join(text_b.lower().split())
        if canonical_a == canonical_b:
            return {"entailment": 0.99, "neutral": 0.005, "contradiction": 0.005}

        self._check_idle_ttl()
        self._load_model()
        if not self._loaded:
            return None
        self._last_used = time.time()

        try:
            # ONNX backend returns logits
            scores = self._model.predict([(text_a, text_b)])
            # Softmax to convert logits to probabilities
            if hasattr(scores, 'tolist'):
                scores = scores.tolist()
            elif hasattr(scores, '__iter__'):
                scores = list(scores)
            else:
                scores = [float(scores)]

            # Handle nested list shape: [[s0, s1, s2]]
            if scores and isinstance(scores[0], list):
                scores = scores[0]

            # Apply softmax
            max_score = max(scores)

def reindex_all(

        entity_types: list[str] | None = None,
        project: str | None = None,
        batch_size: int = 100,
        knowledge_embedding: Any | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, int]:
        """Re-generate embeddings for all entities of the given types.

        This is the canonical reindex implementation used by CLI, MCP, and API.
        Handles batching, per-entity retry on batch failure, and taxonomy
        metadata propagation.

        With multi-model embedding, code entity types (node) use ``self`` (the
        code model), and all other types use ``knowledge_embedding`` if provided.
        Both models must produce the same dimensionality.

        When ``EMBEDDING_SEQUENTIAL_REINDEX`` is enabled (default), the code
        model is loaded, all code entities are embedded, the model is unloaded,
        then the knowledge model is loaded. This halves peak RSS during reindex
        (~850 MB instead of ~1.7 GB) at the cost of not interleaving batches.

        Args:
            storage: Storage instance to read entities from and store embeddings.
            entity_types: Entity types to reindex. Defaults to all embeddable types.
            project: Optional project filter.
            batch_size: Number of entities to embed per batch.
            knowledge_embedding: Optional EmbeddingEngine for non-code entities.
                If None, uses ``self`` for all entity types.

        Returns:

        """
